title: Coca-Cola thinks ‘outside the box,’ books bulk vessels to ship supplies
summary: Coca-Cola is utilizing bulk vessels to transport materials, a non-traditional approach to navigate limited vessel space and keep production lines running globally. This strategy, adopted by other retailers facing supply chain congestion, involves carrying over 60,000 tons of material to non-congested ports to avoid delays and high demurrage fees. While individual company actions may not shift market dynamics, this move highlights the significant impact and overstretched state of current logistics.

title: Top Women in Convenience Awards Gala Honors Change Champions
summary: The 2021 Top Women in Convenience (TWIC) Awards Gala celebrated 74 outstanding women from the convenience store industry, including five Women of the Year. Held in Chicago, the event highlighted themes of resilience, leadership, and the importance of mentorship, particularly for women in historically male-dominated fields. Honorees shared personal reflections on their careers, the impact of COVID-19 on women, and the ongoing progress and challenges in achieving gender equality within the industry.

title: The Coca-Cola Company unveils fresh brand platform for Coca-Cola trademark
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has launched a new global brand platform called "Real Magic" with a refreshed visual identity and logo. This platform aims to celebrate humanity and unite people, building on lessons from the past 18 months, and will be supported by a new campaign blending real and virtual worlds, featuring gamers and interactive elements. The initiative marks the first new global brand platform for Coca-Cola since 2016.

title: Coca-Cola Is Launching This for the First Time in Half a Decade
summary: Coca-Cola is launching a new brand campaign called "Real Magic," featuring a new logo and tagline, for the first time in five years. This rebrand comes amidst declining sales for Classic Coke and the discontinuation of underperforming brands as the company adapts to changing consumer preferences and addresses past criticisms. The campaign aims to connect with a younger, more health-conscious demographic that demands new approaches from the beverage giant.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Announces ESG Presentation for Investors
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced an upcoming webcast for investors on November 3 at 11 a.m. ET to discuss its environmental, social, and governance (ESG) priorities. Bea Perez and Henrique Braun, along with other company leaders, will lead the discussion and a moderated Q&A session. Investors are invited to join the webcast and can review the company's latest Business & ESG Report in advance.

title: Net Zero by 2040
summary: Coca-Cola HBC aims to achieve Net Zero emissions across its entire value chain by 2040, having already reduced direct emissions by 58% and total value chain emissions by a third since 2010. The company's strategy involves significant reductions in direct emissions and collaborative efforts with suppliers to address indirect scope 3 emissions. This commitment is supported by science-based targets validated by SBTi, including renewed climate targets for 2030 and 2040, and targets for Forest, Land and Agriculture (FLAG) emissions.

title: Innovation and Trust: Imperatives in the Emerging Relationship Between Banks & VASPs
summary: The article discusses the growing collaboration between traditional banks and Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) due to the booming cryptocurrency market. It highlights the opportunities for banks to offer new financial products and services while emphasizing the need for thorough due diligence when partnering with VASPs, given the evolving regulatory landscape. The author advises banks to assess a VASP's risk assessment, regulatory compliance, and governance to ensure a successful and secure partnership in the digital asset space.

title: Irish businessman and TV presenter Sir Gerry Robinson dies aged 72
summary: Sir Gerry Robinson, the Donegal-born businessman and television presenter known for his work with Matchbox Toys, Coca-Cola, and Granada Television, has died at the age of 72. He gained public recognition for fronting BBC shows like 'I'll Show Them Who's Boss' and 'Can Gerry Robinson Fix the NHS?', where he advised struggling businesses and hospitals. Knighted in 2004, he had returned to his home county of Donegal in 1996.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA alerta sobre nueva estafa en supuestas ofertas laborales
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA has issued a warning regarding a new scam involving fake job offers that solicit banking information from unsuspecting individuals. The company clarifies that all recruitment processes are conducted solely through official channels and that sensitive financial data is never requested via phone calls or unofficial means. Interested applicants are directed to the official careers website, careers.femsa.com/KOF, to apply for positions and receive employment information.

title: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo wade into booze amid an uncertain future
summary: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo are cautiously entering the alcohol market through partnerships, aiming to learn about the category before fully committing. This move is driven by the search for new growth avenues and higher profit margins, leveraging partners' expertise in the complex alcohol distribution system. Both companies are also subtly exploring potential future ventures into the cannabis market if regulations permit.

title: Birmingham’s Coca-Cola Bottling Company United’s production team wins coveted President’s Award for Quality Excellence
summary: The New Orleans Coca-Cola Production Center, a facility of Birmingham's Coca-Cola Bottling Company United, Inc., has won the prestigious President's Award for Quality Excellence from The Coca-Cola Company. The facility was recognized for its best-in-class performance in reducing consumer complaints and its commitment to quality, even amidst challenges like Hurricane Ida. This achievement highlights the team's resilience and dedication to the company's core values.

title: Pricier shipping containers and port delays haven't slowed Vita Coco's growth, co-CEO says
summary: Vita Coco, despite supply chain challenges and port delays, has continued to grow its business substantially, according to co-founder and co-CEO Mike Kirban. The company went public on Nasdaq under the symbol "COCO," raising $173 million with an initial offering price of $15 per share, although shares fell nearly 4% in afternoon trading. Vita Coco's strong long-term contracts with coconut manufacturers have helped it avoid higher commodity costs, a key differentiator from competitors.

title: Exclusive: Coca-Cola unveils prototype bottle made from 100% plant-based sources
summary: Coca-Cola has revealed a prototype bottle made entirely from 100% plant-based plastic (bPET), a significant step towards reducing dependence on oil-based PET. This innovation leverages commercially scalable technologies and is part of Coca-Cola's broader ambition to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, aiming to use three million tonnes less virgin plastic from oil sources by 2025. The company plans to eliminate oil-based virgin PET from plastic bottles in Europe and Japan by 2030, relying on recycled and renewable materials.

title: The Coca-Cola Company and PepsiCo named top plastic polluters for the fourth year in a row
summary: For the fourth consecutive year, The Coca-Cola Company and PepsiCo have been identified as the world's leading plastic polluters by Break Free From Plastic's annual Brand Audit. The report also highlights Unilever rising to become the third-worst polluter, drawing criticism given its role as a principal partner for COP26. The audit, based on global volunteer cleanups, underscores that these corporations' voluntary commitments are having minimal impact and calls for governments to implement policies to reduce plastic production and hold producers accountable.

title: The Coca‑Cola Company unveils 100% plant-based plastic beverage bottle
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has introduced a prototype beverage bottle made from 100% plant-based plastic, excluding the cap and label. This innovation builds on their 2009 PlantBottle, which contained up to 30% plant-based material. The new bottle utilizes plant-based paraxylene (bPX) from corn sugar and aims for a lower carbon footprint, aligning with Coca-Cola's sustainability goals to use surplus agricultural products.

title: Kraft Heinz CEO: Miguel Patricio Biography
summary: This article provides a biography of Miguel Patricio, the CEO of Kraft Heinz, detailing his career progression from various global CPG companies, through his significant tenure at AB InBev where he focused on marketing and growing the Asia Pacific region, to his current role leading Kraft Heinz's transformation. It highlights his strategies for premiumization, marketing innovation, and fostering creativity to drive growth, along with recent financial performance and strategic asset divestitures under his leadership.

title: Coca-Cola CEO expects to see sporadic product shortages through 2022
summary: Coca-Cola CEO James Quincey anticipates sporadic product shortages to continue through 2022 due to ongoing supply chain challenges and higher inflation. Despite these issues, Coke's earnings and revenue surpassed Wall Street estimates, leading to a 2% rise in share price and an updated fiscal 2021 forecast. Quincey likened the situation to an earthquake with diminishing aftershocks, acknowledging some persistent structural issues.

title: Coca-Cola raises profit forecast as strong soda sales counter cost pressures
summary: Coca-Cola Co raised its full-year profit forecast, driven by higher prices and strong global demand for its sodas. Despite anticipating continued strong demand, CFO John Murphy acknowledged that the company is not immune to cost inflation in 2022 or potential business impacts from new COVID-19 lockdowns. Coca-Cola plans to increase marketing expenditure and prices to navigate these potential challenges.

title: These 10 Stocks Make Up 87% of Warren Buffett's Portfolio
summary: This article details the top 10 stock holdings in Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway portfolio, which collectively account for 87% of its $329.7 billion valuation. It highlights Buffett's belief that diversification isn't essential if one knows their investments well. The individual stocks, including Apple, Bank of America, and Coca-Cola, are discussed with brief explanations for their inclusion and performance.

title: Despite higher prices, McDonald’s, Kraft Heinz and Coca-Cola post solid earnings.
summary: Despite consumers facing higher prices due to supply chain delays and labor shortages, McDonald's, Kraft Heinz, and Coca-Cola all reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings. Their large scale and ability to pass on cost increases to consumers helped them maintain profitability. While some businesses like Kraft Heinz saw a slight decrease in net sales, all three companies demonstrated resilience in a challenging economic environment.

title: Big brands are world’s top plastic polluters for the fourth time
summary: A new study by Break Free from Plastic revealed that major brands like Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Unilever, Nestlé, and P&G are the world's top corporate plastic polluters for the fourth consecutive year. The report, based on audits conducted by volunteers in 45 countries, highlights the continued failure of these companies to adopt sustainable practices despite the climate crisis and the pandemic. Environmental groups are urging lawmakers to pass single-use plastic bans and hold these corporations accountable for their environmental impact.

title: Coca-Cola nearly doubled its advertising this year
summary: Coca-Cola significantly increased its advertising budget this year, nearly doubling it from a year ago. Experts suggest this is a strategic move to maintain "top of mind" awareness among consumers, even for established brands, especially after cutting costs at the pandemic's outset. This advertising also helps combat inflation by allowing price increases while retaining loyal customers.

title: Coca-Cola Unveils 100% Plant-Based PET Bottle, Ready to Scale
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has introduced its first-ever beverage bottle made from 100% plant-based plastic, excluding the cap and label, utilizing two breakthrough technologies ready for commercial scaling. One technology uses sugar from corn to create plant-based terephthalic acid (bPTA), while the other, co-owned with Changchun Meihe Science & Technology, streamlines the production of plant-based monoethylene glycol (bMEG) from sugar sources. This innovation supports Coca-Cola's "World Without Waste" vision to reduce virgin plastic and move towards a circular economy.

title: New York pension fund joins exit from Unilever over Israel restrictions
summary: New York's $268 billion state pension fund has restricted its holdings in Unilever Plc due to sales limits imposed by its Ben & Jerry's brand in Israeli-occupied Palestinian territories. The fund's comptroller stated that a review found Unilever and its subsidiary "engaged in BDS activities." Other U.S. states have taken similar actions following Ben & Jerry's July decision, which Unilever said was made independently and did not signify support for the BDS movement.

title: Coca-Cola Co. offers optimistic outlook
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. reported a strong third quarter with net income rising 42% to $2.5 billion and sales up 16% to $10 billion, leading to an optimistic outlook and raised fiscal 2021 guidance. Despite challenges like uneven global recovery and commodity inflation, the company's chairman and CEO is confident in meeting the goal of emerging stronger from the pandemic. Management expects organic revenue growth of 13% to 14% and comparable EPS growth of 15% to 17% for 2021, and is proactively managing increased costs for 2022.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Acquires Remaining Stake in BODYARMOR
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has acquired full ownership of BODYARMOR, a sports performance and hydration beverage line, for $5.6 billion in cash. This acquisition follows an initial 15% stake purchased in 2018. BODYARMOR will operate as a separate business within Coca-Cola’s North America unit, continuing its strong growth trajectory in the U.S. sports drink category.

title: Coca-Cola is buying sports drink maker BodyArmor
summary: Coca-Cola has acquired sports-drink maker BodyArmor for $5.6 billion, marking its largest brand acquisition to date. This move aims to challenge PepsiCo-owned Gatorade's market dominance and leverage BodyArmor's growing market share. Coca-Cola plans to use both Powerade and BodyArmor to compete more effectively in the expanding sports and performance drinks market.

title: Coca-Cola to fully acquire Gatorade rival BodyArmor for $5.6 bln
summary: Coca-Cola announced it will acquire the remaining stake in BodyArmor for $5.6 billion, intensifying its competition with PepsiCo's Gatorade in the sports drink market. This acquisition is Coca-Cola's largest for a single brand and reflects a strategic shift to bolster its presence in the rapidly growing sports hydration category. BodyArmor, valued at $6.59 billion by the deal, currently boasts $1.4 billion in annual retail sales and a 50% growth rate.

title: Coca-Cola Acquires Full Ownership of BodyArmor
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has completed its acquisition of full ownership of BodyArmor, a sports performance drink, for $5.6 billion in cash. Coca-Cola initially held a 15% stake and will now manage BodyArmor as a separate business unit within its North America operations, retaining BodyArmor's executive leadership. BodyArmor experienced significant growth, with a 25% increase in dollar sales in convenience stores over the past year.

title: Coca-Cola buys rest of BodyArmor for $5.6B in company's largest-ever purchase
summary: Coca-Cola is acquiring the remaining 85% stake in sports drink maker BodyArmor for $5.6 billion, marking its largest acquisition to date. This move strengthens Coca-Cola's position in the sports drink market, where BodyArmor holds an 18% share against PepsiCo's Gatorade. The acquisition aligns with Coca-Cola CEO James Quincey's "total beverage company" strategy, focusing on faster-growing, healthier-positioned products.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Acquires BODYARMOR
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has acquired full ownership of BODYARMOR, a sports performance and hydration beverage brand, for $5.6 billion in cash. Coca-Cola initially bought a 15% stake in 2018 and is now purchasing the remaining 85%. BODYARMOR will operate as a separate business unit within Coca-Cola's North America operations and continue to be based in New York.

title: Coca-Cola Takes Full Ownership Of Bodyarmor For USD$5.6 Billion
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has acquired full ownership of sports drink company BodyArmor for USD$5.6 billion, following an initial 15% stake purchase in 2018. BodyArmor will operate as a separate business within Coca-Cola's U.S. operations, with its co-founder Mike Repole and president Brent Hastie remaining with the company. The acquisition marks Coca-Cola's largest brand purchase to date and comes as BodyArmor has surpassed Powerade in market share.

title: Meet The Markets: Introducing Germany
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) introduces Germany as part of its "Meet the Markets" series, highlighting its long history, operations, and key figures in the country. The article details CCEP's product portfolio, customer reach, sustainability initiatives, and local community investments in Germany. It also shares interesting facts about Fanta and Mezzo Mix, both of which originated in Germany.

title: Splash Beverage Group’s TapouT Performance Drink Gets Rebrand: Enhanced Ergonomic Bottle & Clean Ingredients
summary: Splash Beverage Group is rebranding its TapouT performance hydration-recovery drink, set to launch in January 2022, to broaden its consumer appeal and secure larger distribution networks. The rebrand emphasizes clean ingredients like zero sugar and no artificial sweeteners, and features an ergonomic bottle and dual-language (English and Spanish) labeling. This strategic move aims to leverage the growing performance drink market, following the significant valuation seen in the Body Armor acquisition by Coca-Cola.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Names WPP as Global Marketing Network Partner; Also Appoints Complementary Media Partner
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has named WPP as its Global Marketing Network Partner to drive long-term growth across its brands in over 200 countries. This new integrated agency model aims to transform and modernize marketing and innovation, focusing on consumer-centric, data-driven experiences. Additionally, Dentsu has been appointed as a Complementary Media Partner in select markets, and a Strategic Roster of approved agencies will provide access to creative minds globally.

title: WPP wins Coca-Cola’s massive agency review
summary: WPP has won Coca-Cola's extensive agency review, securing a major account. The decision follows a competitive pitch process for one of the largest marketing accounts in the industry.

title: Coca-Cola company names WPP as global marketing network partner
summary: WPP, the world's largest advertising company, has been named the global marketing network partner for The Coca-Cola Company, a significant win for WPP. This deal includes handling media in eight of Coca-Cola's nine operating units and the majority of its creative work. Coca-Cola also named Dentsu as a complementary media partner and will include Publicis Groupe and IPG in a strategic roster for an open-source creative model.

title: P&G ‘will grind to a halt': Anti-vax group claims to be employees in YouTube video
summary: An anti-vaccination group claiming to be Procter & Gamble employees released a YouTube video protesting the company's vaccine mandate and warning of production shutdowns. P&G announced in September that its 26,000 U.S. employees must provide proof of vaccination, get an exemption, or submit to weekly testing. P&G stated that the video distorts its policy, noting that roughly 75% of its workforce is vaccinated, and is proceeding with compliance with the federal mandate.

title: WPP wins majority of $4 billion Coca-Cola business
summary: WPP has secured the majority of Coca-Cola's $4 billion global marketing business, creating a bespoke unit called OpenX to handle creative, media, data, and marketing technology. Dentsu will act as a complementary media partner in specific geographies like Japan and Korea, while Coca-Cola will also leverage an open-source creative model to tap diverse talent. This major win consolidates Coca-Cola's marketing efforts and represents a significant shift for the involved holding companies.

title: Coca-Cola names WPP global marketing partner
summary: Coca-Cola has appointed WPP as its global marketing network partner following a massive agency review that began in December 2020. A bespoke WPP team, OpenX, will manage end-to-end creative, media, data, and marketing technology across Coca-Cola's entire portfolio, while Dentsu was named a complementary media partner in select markets. This new integrated agency model aims to drive long-term growth and enhance marketing effectiveness and efficiency for the beverage giant.

title: WPP Named Global Marketing Network Partner for Coca-Cola
summary: WPP has been selected as the global marketing network partner for Coca-Cola, winning a significant pitch against rivals such as IPG, Dentsu, and Publicis Groupe. This appointment tasks WPP with driving growth for Coca-Cola's brand portfolio across over 200 countries and territories, as part of Coca-Cola's strategy to modernize its marketing and boost revenue. Coca-Cola's advertising spend was $2.78 billion in 2020, down from previous years.

title: Your guide to Veterans Day free gifts, discounts and events in the Springfield area
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to Veterans Day discounts, free gifts, and events in the Springfield, Missouri area. It lists various businesses offering deals to active military members and veterans, including free food, drinks, discounts on retail, and free haircuts. Additionally, it details several ceremonies and events being held by colleges, universities, and other organizations to honor veterans.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners makes US$15m switch to battery power at UK sites
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) is investing US$15 million to switch to lithium-ion batteries for its equipment, such as forklift trucks, at its UK sites. This move is part of the company's broader goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions. CCEP aims to reduce its carbon footprint and enhance sustainability in its operations.

title: MediaCom Becomes The Coca-Cola Company’s Global Media Agency As Part Of WPP’s OpenX Team
summary: WPP has been chosen as The Coca-Cola Company's Global Marketing Network Partner, with MediaCom serving as the global media agency for the bespoke OpenX team across most markets. This partnership, spanning over 200 markets, aims to transform Coca-Cola’s marketing effectiveness and efficiency starting January 1, 2022. The agreement highlights WPP's integrated capabilities across content, media, data, production, and technology.

title: Walmart asks judge to trash lawsuit over recyclable labeling
summary: Walmart is asking a federal judge to dismiss a renewed lawsuit by Greenpeace alleging the retail giant deceives California consumers by labeling some house-brand plastic products as recyclable. Walmart argues that Greenpeace still lacks standing to sue, claiming the environmental group has not shown it suffered direct harm from the alleged deception. This lawsuit is part of a broader trend of legal actions challenging the recyclability claims of single-use plastic products, with other companies like Keurig Green Mountain and Coca-Cola facing similar complaints.

title: Anti-Woke ETFs Are Pitching to Conservatives Mad at Corporate America
summary: 2ndVote Advisers, led by former JPMorgan Chase & Co. banker Dan Grant, is launching exchange-traded funds (ETFs) aimed at conservative investors who are displeased with companies taking liberal stances on social justice issues. Grant believes that the millions of Trump voters are ready to invest in companies that align with politically conservative values or remain neutral, pushing back against the trend of left-leaning socially conscious investing. This initiative attempts to blend politics and investing by catering to those who feel neglected by "woke" corporations.

title: Asia’s Largest Food Co., Coca-Cola Bottler, and Others Drop Animal Tests
summary: PETA announced that Uni-President, Asia's largest food company, and Swire Coca-Cola Taiwan have banned animal testing not legally required, following discussions with PETA. Additionally, Yakult U.S.A. confirmed that Yakult Co., Ltd. is now included in a parent company policy banning such tests. These companies had previously conducted or funded experiments involving mutilating and killing over 1,200 animals since 2000.

title: Bloomin' Brands and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Team Up For A Hometown Partnership
summary: Bloomin' Brands, Inc. and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers announced a multi-year partnership, bringing together two Tampa Bay staples. This agreement includes marketing rights for Bloomin' Brands' portfolio of restaurants and features an Aussie Grill concession stand at Raymond James Stadium. To celebrate, Outback Steakhouse is offering exclusive Buccaneers souvenir tumblers at participating Tampa Bay locations.

title: DoubleVerify acquires OpenSlate to strengthen CTV, social video targeting
summary: DoubleVerify has acquired OpenSlate, a contextual targeting platform for CTV and social video, in a cash and stock transaction valued at $150 million. This acquisition aims to provide marketers with an end-to-end solution for optimizing their advertising efforts by combining OpenSlate's pre-campaign tools with DoubleVerify's post-flight measurement suite. The deal highlights the growing demand for alternatives to third-party cookies and strengthens DoubleVerify's position in the rapidly expanding social video and CTV markets.

title: Femsa compra otra empresa de distribución en Estados Unidos
summary: Femsa, through its subsidiary Envoy Solutions, has acquired Next-Gen Supply Group, a distribution company in Massachusetts. This acquisition is part of Femsa's strategy to build a leading national distribution platform in the United States, following other recent purchases like Daycon Products and Penn Jersey Paper. Next-Gen Supply Group reported over $90 million in revenue in the 12 months leading up to October 2021.

title: Google consolidates global media account with WPP's Essence without a pitch
summary: Google has consolidated its entire multibillion-dollar global media account with WPP's Essence, including both digital and offline media buying. Previously, Omnicom Media Group handled the offline portion of Google's media business. This consolidation, done without a formal pitch, aims to simplify Google's agency relationships and is a significant win for Essence given its historical focus on digital and programmatic media.

title: Assessing the rise of RTD cocktails, decline of hard seltzer with CANTEEN Spirits CEO
summary: This article discusses the rise of ready-to-drink (RTD) cocktails coinciding with a decline in hard seltzer popularity, as observed by CANTEEN Spirits CEO, Brandon Cason. It highlights how RTD cocktails are driving significant growth in the off-premise spirits market due to consumer demand for convenient, low-ABV options, while hard seltzer sales are slowing after a period of rapid expansion. The piece emphasizes the increasing variety and projected continued growth of RTDs, with canned cocktails expected to exceed $2 billion in the US by 2022.

title: Exponential Growth Expected for Adult Nappy Market With Complete SWOT Analysis by Forecast From 2021 to 2027: Kimberly Clark, SCA, Unicharm, Hartmann
summary: The Adult Nappy Market is expected to see exponential growth between 2021 and 2027, according to a report by Worldwide Market Reports. The report provides detailed insights into market shares, growth opportunities, and competitive landscape, profiling key players like Kimberly Clark, SCA, and Unicharm. It also analyzes the impact of COVID-19 and offers growth prospects across various segments and regions.

title: Diageo's Guinness Chocolate Mint Stout Aged in Kentucky Bourbon Barrels - Product Launch
summary: Diageo's Guinness brand has launched a new Chocolate Mint Stout aged in Kentucky Bourbon Barrels as part of its fourth-year barrel-aged beer project. This limited-edition, 10.8% abv stout, brewed at the Open Gate Brewery in Baltimore, features flavours of dried mint leaves and cacao. It is available nationwide in the US off-premise channel, retailing at $19.99 for a four-pack.

title: Last Call: Ball Can Prices to Increase; Hawaii Stream Register 1.2% ABV
summary: Ball Corporation is significantly increasing can prices and minimum order quantities for craft brewers, with 12 oz. cans rising by nearly 28% and 16 oz. cans by 19.5%, leading to concerns within the Brewers Association about the impact on small brewers. This comes amidst a surge in can demand and supply chain issues. Additionally, the article reports on the death of Anthony Angotti, founder of Beers of the World, and a stream in Oahu, Hawaii registering 1.2% ABV due to contamination from a beverage warehouse spill.

title: Unilever to sell Lipton Tea owner to CVC Capital for $5 Billion
summary: Unilever is selling its tea business, ekaterra, which includes brands like Lipton and PG tips, to CVC Capital Partners for 4.5 billion euros ($5.1 billion). This sale is part of Unilever CEO Alan Jope's strategy to refocus the company's portfolio on higher-growth areas and follows a period of declining demand for traditional tea. The transaction is expected to be completed in the second half of 2022.

title: Monster Beverage exploring deal with Constellation Brands, Bloomberg reports
summary: Monster Beverage is reportedly in discussions with Constellation Brands, the brewer of Modelo and Corona, regarding a potential deal. The exact structure of the tie-up remains uncertain, with possibilities ranging from a full merger to an asset deal, and it could create a beverage powerhouse worth nearly $100 billion. The potential partnership could also explore the CBD market, leveraging Constellation's investment in cannabis company Canopy Growth, and analysts suggest a hard seltzer agreement would be mutually beneficial given both companies' past challenges in the segment.

title: Energy drinks maker Monster Beverage discussing merger with Constellation Brands, source says
summary: Energy drinks maker Monster Beverage Corp is reportedly discussing a merger with international beverage alcohol company Constellation Brands Inc. The potential deal involves companies with a combined market value of nearly $92-billion, although the structure of the deal is not yet known. Both companies have significant market capitalization, with Monster Beverage at $47.3-billion and Constellation Brands at $44.2-billion as of Friday.

title: 20-Year Returns: Monster Eats Apple for Breakfast
summary: Over the past 20 years, Monster Beverage Corporation's stock has outperformed major tech companies like Apple and Amazon, increasing by over 100,000 percent. The company, an early entrant in the energy drink market, has grown significantly, recording $1.4 billion in profit on $4.6 billion in sales in 2020. Monster Beverage is now a dominant player in the energy drink market and has recently been in merger talks with Constellation Brands.

title: Campbell Soup names Lindsay vp/corporate responsibility, sustainability
summary: Campbell Soup Co. has appointed Stewart Lindsay as Vice President, Corporate Responsibility and Sustainability, effective December 6, 2021. Lindsay will report to Adam Ciongoli, Executive Vice President, General Counsel, and Chief Sustainability, Corporate Responsibility, and Governance Officer. Before joining Campbell Soup, Lindsay served as Managing Director of Corporate Engagement at The Nature Conservancy for two years.

title: Ulysses 'Junior' Bridgeman shares insights on navigating the rise to success in the Dec. 8 Business Forum
summary: Former NBA player Ulysses 'Junior' Bridgeman, now president/CEO of Heartland Coca-Cola, will share his journey from a $350,000 salary to a $600 million business empire in the December 8th 21st Century Business Forum webcast. Bridgeman transitioned from basketball to owning over 450 restaurants, including Wendy's and Chili's, and now leads Coca-Cola operations and recently acquired Jet and Ebony magazines. The free webcast, presented by Vermont Business Magazine and sponsored by NBT Bank, will cover his strategies for success.

title: IHG Hotels & Resorts and Coca-Cola unveil "Santa's Suite Retreat" in countdown to Christmas
summary: IHG Hotels & Resorts and Coca-Cola have partnered to introduce "Santa's Suite Retreat" at select InterContinental properties in New York and Atlanta, along with a presidential suite at Crowne Plaza Atlanta Perimeter at Ravinia for IHG Rewards members. These holiday-themed suites aim to provide guests with a magical, Santa-inspired experience to foster togetherness during the festive season. Bookings open on December 9th at santasuiteretreat.com.

title: Coca-Cola HBC again recognised by CDP with double ‘A’ score for global climate action and water stewardship
summary: Coca-Cola HBC has received a double 'A' rating from CDP for its efforts in climate action and water stewardship for the sixth and fifth consecutive year, respectively. This recognition places them among the top 1% of over 13,000 businesses assessed by CDP. The company has also committed to achieving net-zero emissions across its entire value chain by 2040, investing €250 million in reduction initiatives by 2025.

title: Coca-Cola and others report using more recycled plastic
summary: Major packaged goods companies, including Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Unilever, reported increased use of post-consumer recycled (PCR) plastic in 2020, according to a report by the Ellen MacArthur Foundation. While these companies are making progress toward their 2025 targets, many still have significant ground to cover. Greenpeace, however, criticized the focus on recycled content, arguing that it does not solve the fundamental problem of plastic pollution and encourages continued fossil fuel-based plastic production.

title: Coca-Cola Launches Its First U.S. TikTok Challenge
summary: Coca-Cola has launched its inaugural U.S. TikTok challenge, #ShareTheMagic, leveraging the platform's massive user base of over 1 billion monthly active users. The campaign features Grammy-nominated artist Khalid, whose new song "Open" serves as the soundtrack, encouraging users to showcase their unique talents. As of noon ET on the day of the article's publication, the hashtag had already garnered more than 90 million views.

title: Pressure mounts to strip Activision’s chief of his seat on Coca-Cola’s board. (Published 2021)
summary: A union-led investment group, SOC Investment Group, plans to ask Coca-Cola not to renominate Activision Blizzard CEO Bobby Kotick to its board, citing accusations of sexual misconduct and discrimination at Activision. This push follows earlier calls for Kotick to resign from Activision and comes as Coca-Cola emphasizes its commitment to diversity and inclusion. If Coca-Cola retains Kotick, SOC threatens to oppose the re-election of other directors.

title: VIDEO: Triumphs on Display at 2021 Top Women in Convenience Awards Gala
summary: The 2021 Top Women in Convenience (TWIC) Awards Gala celebrated resilience, strength, innovation, and triumph among 74 exceptional women in the convenience store industry. This year marked a record number of honorees, including five Women of the Year, who were recognized for their significant contributions to their companies and the industry overall. The gala, held in Chicago alongside the NACS Show, highlighted leaders from retailer, distributor, and supplier communities.

title: Kraft Heinz Hires Abbott Exec to Lead R&D
summary: The Kraft Heinz Co. has appointed Robert Scott as president of research & development – North America, effective Dec. 8, as the company prepares to combine its U.S. and Canada businesses. Scott, formerly of Abbott Nutrition and The Coca-Cola Co., will lead R&D for Kraft Heinz's core business, renovation, innovation, and commercialization strategy. This move aims to advance Kraft Heinz's North America portfolio strategy with a focus on sustainable solutions.

title: Minute Maid products recalled in 8 states because of metal pieces
summary: The Coca Cola Company has issued a recall for certain Minute Maid products across eight states due to potential contamination with foreign objects, specifically metal bolts or washers. The affected products include Minute Maid Berry Punch, Strawberry Lemonade, and Fruit Punch, distributed in Pennsylvania, Connecticut, New York, North Carolina, Maryland, Virginia, Maine, and New Jersey. Consumers are advised not to use these products, as their long shelf life means some may still be in homes.

title: Why Vita Coco and Zico founders are betting on coconut water’s comeback
summary: Despite a decline in popularity for coconut water, the founders of major brands Vita Coco and Zico are making significant moves to revitalize the market. Zico's founder, Mark Rampolla, bought his brand back from Coca-Cola and is reintroducing it to stores, while Vita Coco is launching an initial public offering (IPO) aiming to raise $224 million and is actively engaging consumers with a quirky social media presence. Both founders are personally invested in the product, having discovered its benefits and having compelling origin stories that fuel their belief in coconut water's enduring potential.

title: Merger rumour: Monster and Constellation to create total beverage firm
summary: A merger rumor suggests that Monster Beverage and Constellation Brands are exploring a deal to create a "total beverage company" encompassing energy drinks, spirits, beer, RTDs, and potentially cannabis. This potential megadeal would be one of the largest in the beverage industry, though Coca-Cola's stake in Monster and investor skepticism pose complexities. The concept aims to energize beverage giants to find new ways to engage consumers.

title: Recall: ‘Foreign matter’ potentially in some Coca-Cola soda, juices
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has issued two separate recalls for some of its Minute Maid juices and Coca-Cola and Sprite sodas due to the potential presence of "foreign matter." The Minute Maid juices may contain washers and metal bolts, while the soda cans also have an unspecified foreign matter issue. Consumers are advised to dispose of the affected products.

title: Coca-Cola recall: Officials say some juices, canned soda may contain metal
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has issued two recalls for several of its Minute Maid juices and canned sodas due to the potential presence of "foreign matter," specifically washers and metal bolts. Consumers are advised to check their refrigerators and dispose of or return affected products for a full refund. The recalled items were distributed across various states in the Northeast and Southeast.

title: Atlanta artist leads Coca-Cola's TikTok debut with #ShareTheMagic challenge
summary: Coca-Cola made its TikTok debut with the #ShareTheMagic challenge featuring Atlanta-based artist Jalaiah Harmon and singer Khalid. Harmon choreographed an original dance to Khalid's song "Open," with her video amassing over 7 million views. The challenge aims to engage content creators and elevate emerging talent by celebrating diverse passion points.

title: ‘Diet’ soda is disappearing from store shelves - Boston News, Weather, Sports
summary: The term "diet" is being phased out on soda packaging, replaced by "zero sugar," as beverage companies aim to appeal to younger consumers, particularly Millennials and Gen Z-ers, who view the word "diet" negatively. Despite the rebranding, the no-calorie soft drink market is growing rapidly, with sales up 19.5% since 2018. This shift reflects evolving attitudes towards dieting and health, encouraging soda makers to highlight the absence of sugar as a positive attribute.

title: ‘Keurig for cocktails’ abruptly decides to shutter operations
summary: Drinkworks, a joint venture between Anheuser-Busch and Keurig Dr Pepper that offered an at-home cocktail machine, announced it is ceasing operations and sales immediately. Customers have until February 28, 2022, to apply for reimbursements for their systems, and cocktail pods will be available until March 31, 2022. The decision comes despite the company experiencing a boost in sales during the COVID-19 pandemic due to increased at-home consumption.

title: Karla Radtke Named Coke Florida Vice President, Chief of Staff
summary: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida, LLC (Coke Florida) has appointed Karla Radtke as Vice President and Chief of Staff to Chairman and CEO Troy Taylor. Radtke brings nearly 30 years of experience within the Coca-Cola system, having held various roles in sales, marketing, and supply chain across multiple Coca-Cola entities. She will play a key role in the company's growth strategy and collaborate closely with leadership.

title: Activist Investing Today: R5’s Mushkin Talks Dollar Tree, Hain
summary: Scott Mushkin of R5 Capital discusses Mantle Ridge's activism at Dollar Tree, comparing its new pricing strategy to Coca-Cola's "New Coke" failure due to potential brand dilution. He also addresses Hain Celestial's M&A strategy, suggesting a sale to a large packaged foods company is unlikely in the near future despite potential receptiveness to reasonable offers. Mushkin emphasizes Dollar Tree's underperformance relative to competitors and the S&P 500, indicating Mantle Ridge's potential success.

title: Herbert A. Allen III Elected to Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: Herbert A. Allen III, president of Allen & Co. LLC, has been elected to The Coca-Cola Company's board of directors, effective December 17, 2021. Allen, 54, follows his father, Herbert A. Allen Jr., who retired after 39 years on the board. His appointment expands the Coca-Cola board to 12 directors.

title: Herbert A. Allen III Elected to Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: Herbert A. Allen III, president of Allen & Co. LLC, has been elected to the Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company, effective December 17. He brings nearly two decades of experience leading Allen & Co., an investment firm focused on media, entertainment, and technology. Allen's father, Herbert A. Allen Jr., retired from the Coca-Cola board earlier in the year after 39 years of service, continuing a long-standing relationship between Allen & Co. and The Coca-Cola Company.

title: Ana Callol to become Chief Public Affairs, Communications and Sustainability Officer
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) announced that Ana Callol will take on the role of Chief Public Affairs, Communications and Sustainability Officer, succeeding Lauren Sayeski. Callol, with over 20 years in the Coca-Cola system, is expected to accelerate CCEP's "This is Forward" sustainability plan. Sayeski will transition to a new position at The Coca-Cola Company.

title: Herbert A. Allen III Elected to Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: Herbert A. Allen III, president of Allen & Co. LLC, has been elected to the Board of Directors of The Coca-Cola Company, effective December 17, 2021. Allen brings deep knowledge and valuable perspective from his nearly two decades leading Allen & Co., a privately held investment firm focused on media, entertainment, and technology. His father, Herbert A. Allen Jr., retired from the Coca-Cola board earlier in the year after 39 years of service.

title: Mercado de cerveza de Chile enfrenta alta competencia
summary: The Chilean beer market is highly competitive, featuring a wide range of local and imported beers, with CCU's main competitor being Cervecería Chile, a subsidiary of Ambev S.A. Other key players include Viña Concha y Toro SA and Cooperativa Agrícola Pisquera Elqui Limitada (Capel), which import international brands and produce craft beer. The article also touches upon the competition in the non-alcoholic beverages segment, where CCU faces off against licensees of The Coca-Cola Company.

title: Wheels Up Appoints Stevens Sainte-Rose as Chief People Officer
summary: Wheels Up Experience Inc. (NYSE:UP) has appointed Stevens J. Sainte-Rose as its new Chief People Officer. In this role, he will oversee all human resources and cultural aspects, including organizational design, talent acquisition, development, retention, and diversity and inclusion. Sainte-Rose brings extensive HR experience from various industries, with previous roles at The Coca-Cola Company International, U.S. Walgreens, Dawn Foods Global, and Parallel Inc.

title: Live Nation Backs Liquid Death In New $75 Million Funding Round
summary: Live Nation has once again invested in Liquid Death, a canned water company, through a new $75 million Series C funding round. This brings Liquid Death's total funding to $125 million and values the brand at $525 million. The funding will further support the growth of Liquid Death, which has significantly increased its distribution and revenue, leveraging its exclusivity at Live Nation venues and festivals.

title: Southern Railway Serves the South
summary: The Atlanta History Center received a significant collection of railroad archival materials from Norfolk Southern Corporation, including corporate records from Southern Railway and over 200 forerunner companies, and a $500,000 donation for archiving and digitization. The collection highlights Southern Railway's pivotal role in developing the South, its technological innovations, and its impact on Atlanta as a major transportation hub. These newly acquired archives will help tell the story of the many people and businesses connected to the railroads.

title: More than words
summary: Plastic packaging producers worldwide are increasing investments to close the loop on their products, acknowledging the historically low recycling rates for plastic compared to other materials. These investments span various forms, from traditional scrap collection and processing to advanced recycling technologies, driven by regulatory pressure, corporate sustainability goals, and shareholder activism. The article highlights major players like Alpla Group, Amcor, Sealed Air Corp., Ineos Styrolution, and PureCycle Technologies, emphasizing efforts in PET, HDPE, and PP, and discussing the debate around the economic viability and environmental impact of chemical recycling.

title: Constellation Brands partners with Coca Cola on new ready-to-drink cocktail FRESCA Mixed
summary: Constellation Brands has announced a partnership with Coca-Cola to produce and distribute FRESCA Mixed, a new ready-to-drink cocktail. This venture aims to tap into the growing "Adult Alternative Beverages" market, estimated at nearly $8 billion, by combining Fresca's popular branding with Constellation's expertise in spirits. The new product is expected to launch this year, further solidifying Constellation's presence in the beverage industry and following their recent decision to relocate headquarters to Rochester, N.Y.

title: Constellation Brands and Coca-Cola Partner on Fresca Branded Spirits-Based RTD
summary: Constellation Brands has teamed up with The Coca-Cola Company to launch Fresca Mixed, a spirits-based ready-to-drink cocktail derived from the popular Fresca soft drink. This collaboration leverages Fresca's rapidly growing consumer base and Constellation's expertise in beverage alcohol to create a new product expected to be released later this year. This initiative follows Coca-Cola's previous foray into RTDs with Molson Coors for Topo Chico Hard Seltzer.

title: Coca-Cola and Constellation Brands team up to create alcoholic Fresca cocktails
summary: Coca-Cola and Constellation Brands are collaborating to launch spirits-based Fresca Mixed Cocktails in the U.S. this year. This partnership leverages Fresca's growing popularity and existing use as a cocktail mixer, aiming to capture a share of the expanding canned cocktails market. This marks Coca-Cola's second venture into alcoholic beverages since the 1980s, following the successful Topo Chico Hard Seltzer.

title: P&G takes first step into the metaverse with BeautySphere
summary: P&G Beauty has entered the metaverse with the launch of BeautySphere, a virtual storytelling world accessible via desktop, which debuted at CES. This platform enables consumers to interact with P&G's brands through live content, panel discussions, and gamified challenges, focusing on the company's "Responsible Beauty" initiatives. BeautySphere aims to engage digitally-savvy consumers on a nascent virtual landscape, bridging virtual experiences with real-world impact, such as planting trees for reforestation efforts.

title: Constellation Brands enters agreement with Coca-Cola, Fresca to launch line of alcohol
summary: Constellation Brands has partnered with Coca-Cola to launch "Fresca Mixed," a new line of spirit-based, ready-to-drink cocktails. This collaboration aims to capitalize on Fresca's growing popularity and Constellation Brands' expertise in the alcoholic beverage industry. The new product line is expected to launch in 2022 and aligns with emerging consumer trends.

title: Coca-Cola, Constellation Brands strike deal to offer Fresca canned cocktails
summary: Coca-Cola is partnering with Constellation Brands to launch a new line of spirit-based, ready-to-drink canned cocktails under its Fresca brand, called Fresca Mixed, which is expected to debut later this year. This collaboration follows similar moves by other beverage giants into the adult alternative beverage market, a rapidly growing segment. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed, and Constellation Brands will be responsible for production, marketing, and distribution.

title: Constellation Brands Grows Shipments +3%, Depletions +8% in Q3; Brewery Expansions to Add 20+ Million Barrels of Capacity
summary: Constellation Brands reported strong Q3 results for its beer business, with shipments up 3.1% and depletions up 8.4%. The company plans significant brewery expansions in Mexico, investing up to $5.5 billion to add over 20 million barrels of capacity, aiming for 7-9% top-line growth in beer. Despite margin declines due to increased costs, Constellation expects to implement price increases and is launching a new spirits-based canned cocktail, Fresca Mixed, through its wholesaler network.

title: Constellation Brands, Coca-Cola enter agreement for FRESCA brand
summary: Constellation Brands and The Coca-Cola Co. have announced a brand authorization agreement in the U.S. to launch FRESCA Mixed, a new line of spirit-based, ready-to-drink (RTD) cocktails. This collaboration aims to leverage the growing adult alternative beverage market, with FRESCA Mixed products expected to hit the market later this year. The initiative builds on FRESCA's rising popularity as a mixer and a sparkling soda, using Constellation's expertise in beverage alcohol.

title: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida Names James Boyce as Territory General Manager
summary: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida (Coke Florida) has promoted James "Jim" Boyce to Territory General Manager for its Tampa territory, effective January 15, 2022. Boyce brings 23 years of experience in the CPG industry, having previously served as Plant Manager for Coke Florida’s Tampa Manufacturing facility. In his new role, he will be responsible for local business outcomes and coordinating functional teams in the Tampa market, which is one of the company's largest territories.

title: Constellation Brands to Launch Fresca Spirit-Based Beverages
summary: Coca-Cola has partnered with Constellation Brands to launch Fresca Mixed, a new line of spirit-based, ready-to-drink (RTD) cocktails in the U.S. Fresca, traditionally used as a mixer, will be marketed and distributed by Constellation Brands, known for Corona and Modelo. This move taps into the growing RTD cocktail market, which is projected to see significant growth.

title: Constellation Brands strikes deal to bring Coca-Cola’s new beverage alcohol product to market
summary: Coca-Cola has partnered with Constellation Brands to launch Fresca Mixed, a new line of spirit-based ready-to-drink (RTD) cocktails in the United States. Constellation Brands will handle the manufacturing, marketing, and distribution of these new alcoholic beverages. This move allows Coca-Cola to expand its "total beverage company" goal, tapping into the growing adult alternative beverage market, which is projected to grow 15-17% CAGR over the next three years.

title: Cocktail start-up Drinkworks closes amidst disappointing sales
summary: Drinkworks, a joint venture between AB InBev and Keurig Dr Pepper, has ceased sales of its countertop cocktail-making machines due to disappointing sales. The company will refund customers who purchased the appliance, and cocktail pods and accessories will be sold until March. This closure follows a similar unsuccessful venture by Keurig with Coca-Cola Co. to sell soft drink machines.

title: New Report Shows Continued Growth in Hard Seltzer Market
summary: A new report projects the global hard seltzer market to reach USD 49.4 billion by 2028, growing at a CAGR of 31.4% from 2021 to 2028. This growth is driven by shifting consumer preferences for low-alcohol, low-calorie

title: Lehigh Valley Coca-Cola strike continues into 2nd month after union vote fails
summary: The strike at the Lehigh Valley Coca-Cola bottling and distribution plant has extended into its second month after Teamsters Local 773 rejected a proposed compromise. Workers began picketing on December 6 over changes to healthcare plans and the move from pensions to 401(k)s. ABARTA Coca-Cola Beverages states it offered drastically reduced employee premium costs, new coverage options, and faster wage increases, which the union rejected.

title: How C-stores Are Raising the Bar in Alcoholic Beverages
summary: The convenience store channel is seeing a significant rise in wine and liquor sales, largely driven by the pandemic, prompting stores like Parker's, Casey's General Stores, and 7‑Eleven to innovate their offerings. Industry insiders predict continued growth in these categories, emphasizing the importance of clear communication, strategic displays, and diverse product selections—including single-serve and ready-to-drink options—to meet evolving consumer demands and maximize sales.

title: John Murphy to Become President and Chief Financial Officer of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced that John Murphy, currently Executive Vice President and CFO, will assume the role of President and Chief Financial Officer on October 1. This change follows the retirement of Brian Smith, who has served as President and Chief Operating Officer since 2019. Murphy will expand his responsibilities to include oversight of Global Ventures, Platform Services, digital transformation, and customer and commercial leadership.

title: People on the move: January 2022
summary: This article highlights new appointments and changes in the beverage industry during January 2022. Key personnel movements include Anne-Marie D’Angelo joining Molson Coors as Chief Legal and Government Affairs Officer, new members appointed to the Brewers Association Board of Directors, Brian Perkins becoming President of Budweiser Brewing Group UK&I, and CSR appointments at Typhoo Tea. Pernod Ricard USA also expanded its government relations team with two new executives.

title: Monster Beverage Is Making A Huge Move Into The Alcohol Sector With The Purchase Of CANarchy
summary: Monster Beverage (MNST) has acquired CANarchy Craft Brewery Collective for $330 million, officially entering the alcohol beverage market. This acquisition provides Monster with established distribution networks and existing infrastructure to launch new alcoholic products. The deal comes as the hard seltzer market continues to grow and other beverage companies are merging into the alcohol sector.

title: Coca-Cola HBC AG completes acquisition of majority stake in Coca-Cola Bottling Company of Egypt
summary: Coca-Cola Hellenic Bottling Company (Coca-Cola HBC) has finalized its acquisition of a 52.7% stake in Coca-Cola Bottling Company of Egypt (CCBCE) for $304 million. This move grants Coca-Cola HBC access to the second-largest non-alcoholic ready-to-drink market in Africa, aiming to leverage its market experience to increase brand penetration. An additional 2.8% stake may be acquired from other minority shareholders, and further acquisition from The Coca-Cola Company is expected to bring Coca-Cola HBC's total ownership to 94.7%.

title: Coca-Cola HBC AG completes the acquisition of a majority stake in Coca-Cola Bottling Company of Egypt
summary: Coca-Cola HBC AG has announced the completion of its acquisition of approximately 52.7% of Coca-Cola Bottling Company of Egypt (CCBCE) from MAC Beverages Limited for $304 million. This acquisition, which is expected to increase Coca-Cola HBC's total ownership in CCBCE to 94.7% later this month, provides Coca-Cola HBC with access to Egypt's significant non-alcoholic ready-to-drink market. The company plans to leverage its expertise to drive growth and penetration of The Coca-Cola Company's brand portfolio in the region.

title: Coca-Cola Burj Khalifa Advertising | Coca-Cola Middle East
summary: The Coca‑Cola Company unveiled its new global philosophy, "Real Magic," with a spectacular light show on the Burj Khalifa in Dubai. The event celebrated human connection and showcased moments that unite and uplift people. This philosophy, along with a refreshed visual identity, emphasizes finding magic in unexpected everyday moments and the value of diversity.

title: Monster Beverage to buy craft-beer maker in alcohol market drive
summary: Monster Beverage Corp is entering the alcoholic drinks market by acquiring CANarchy Craft Brewery Collective LLC for $330 million. This all-cash deal signifies a broader trend of soft-drink companies expanding into the alcohol sector, providing Monster with established infrastructure and expertise in the industry. The acquisition adds several craft beer brands to Monster's portfolio and is expected to close in the first quarter of this year.

title: Monster acquires CANarchy, which includes Cigar City & Oskar Blues
summary: Monster Beverage Corp, known for Monster Energy Drinks, has acquired CANarchy, a craft beer collective that includes Oskar Blues and Cigar City Brewing, in a $330 million all-cash deal. This acquisition grants Monster access to an established craft brewing infrastructure and distribution channels, ahead of its planned entry into the alcoholic beverage industry with new products and hard seltzers. The Brewers Association has stated that CANarchy will retain its "craft brewer" definition under Monster's ownership, as Monster is not currently a beverage alcohol industry member.

title: New Mutation — Monster Energy Finds National Alcohol Foothold in CANarchy Acquisition
summary: Monster Beverage Corporation is acquiring CANarchy Craft Brewery Collective LLC for $330 million in cash, marking Monster's entry into the alcohol market. This deal provides Monster with a national alcohol distribution network and production capabilities, while Fireman Capital Partners, CANarchy's owner, secures a return on investment amidst a challenging sales market for craft beer. The acquisition is seen as a strategic move for Monster to diversify its portfolio, potentially moving away from a rumored merger with Constellation Brands.

title: Monster Energy Acquires CANarchy for $330M, Entering the Alcohol Industry
summary: Monster Beverage Corp. has announced its acquisition of craft beer and hard seltzer producer CANarchy Brewery Collective, LLC for $330 million, marking its official entry into the alcoholic beverage industry. This move follows a trend of soft beverage companies expanding into alcohol, much like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo. The acquisition is expected to close before the end of the first quarter and provides Monster with an established infrastructure for alcoholic beverage development and distribution.

title: Monster Energy enters alcohol with $330M purchase of Canarchy Craft Brewery
summary: Monster Beverage is set to acquire Canarchy Craft Brewery Collective for $330 million, marking its entry into the alcoholic beverage market. This strategic move provides Monster with an established infrastructure and brands like Cigar City and Oskar Blues, allowing it to diversify beyond energy drinks and compete with industry giants. The acquisition comes amidst rumors of Monster itself being an acquisition target, suggesting a push towards independence and new growth avenues.

title: Your Favorite Craft Beer May Now Be Owned By Monster Beverage
summary: Monster Beverage Corp has acquired CANarchy Craft Brewery Collective in a $330 million deal, marking its entry into the alcoholic beverage market. This move allows Monster to leverage established craft beer and hard seltzer brands like Oskar Blues and Cigar City, rather than creating new ones from scratch. The energy drink company plans for Monster and CANarchy to operate independently, with potential future Monster-branded alcoholic beverages.

title: Monster Beverage to enter alcohol market with craft beer
summary: Monster Beverage Corp is venturing into the alcoholic drinks market through a US$330 million acquisition of CANarchy Craft Brewery Collective LLC. This move allows Monster, known for its energy drinks, to gain infrastructure, distribution, and expertise in the alcoholic beverage industry. The deal, expected to close in the first quarter of the year, reflects a trend of soft-drink companies expanding into alcohol.

title: ThredUp appoints Coretha Rushing to its board of directors
summary: ThredUp has appointed Coretha Rushing to its board of directors, leveraging her 35 years of human resources experience. Rushing will advise the company on employee initiatives, including health and wellness, attraction, retention, and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB). Her expertise is expected to be invaluable as ThredUp continues to expand and manage its global workforce.

title: The 10 Best Consumer Cyclical Stocks to Buy for 2022
summary: This article identifies the top 10 consumer cyclical stocks to consider buying in 2022, based on the expectation of robust economic growth and strong consumer confidence. It highlights companies in recreation, retail, household durables, automotive, and media sectors, detailing their recent financial performance, stock movements, and market outlook. The list includes companies like Chewy, Coca-Cola, Costco, Ford, Home Depot, Nike, and Royal Caribbean, along with two relevant ETFs.

title: Coca-Cola refreshes can designs to highlight flavor portfolio
summary: Coca-Cola has updated the packaging for its flavored and zero-sugar products to make it easier for consumers to differentiate between flavors and sugar content. The redesign uses full-color cans for single flavors and stacked colors for dual flavors, with a white Coca-Cola logo for full-sugar drinks and a black logo for zero-sugar options. This refresh is part of a broader strategy to simplify its growing product range and expand into new consumption occasions, like the afternoon "pick-me-up" market, through products like Coca-Cola with Coffee Mocha and exploring innovative delivery methods.

title: Coca-Cola Won't Air a Super Bowl Ad for Second Year in a Row
summary: For the second consecutive year, Coca-Cola has decided not to run an ad during the Super Bowl, choosing instead to focus its marketing efforts on existing sports sponsorships like NCAA March Madness and the Daytona 500. This decision allows the company to further concentrate on rebuilding its agency partnerships and adapting its advertising strategy, especially as it navigates changing consumer preferences towards healthier beverage options. The soft drink giant will also be able to dedicate more attention to its presence at the Beijing Olympics.

title: One Lawsuit Settled, Another Filed Over Plan Investments in Fidelity TDFs
summary: A lawsuit against Coca-Cola Consolidated's 401(k) plan fiduciaries regarding their investment in actively managed Fidelity Freedom Funds TDFs has reached a settlement. Simultaneously, the same law firm has filed an identical lawsuit against DISH Network Corp.'s 401(k) plan fiduciaries, also alleging unreasonable recordkeeping and administrative fees. Both cases argue that the index version of Fidelity's TDFs would have been a superior option for plan participants.

title: Molson Coors and Coca-Cola Expand Partnership to Bring New Alcoholic Juice Product to The Market
summary: Molson Coors and The Coca-Cola Company have expanded their partnership to launch Simply Spiked Lemonade™, an alcoholic juice product inspired by Coca-Cola's Simply® brand. This collaboration follows the successful introduction of Topo Chico® Hard Seltzer and aims to disrupt the full-flavor alcohol segment. Simply Spiked Lemonade will be available in a variety pack featuring popular Simply® flavors and marks a significant step in Molson Coors' strategy to grow its above-premium portfolio.

title: South Africa and Africa’s Top Employers 2022
summary: In 2022, 249 organizations across 31 African countries achieved Top Employer certification due to their outstanding HR strategies. Unilever, JTI, and Vodacom were recognized as the top three employers in Africa. Unilever South Africa, Accenture (South Africa), and Vodacom Group led the list for South Africa, with various companies also achieving industry leader recognition in specific sectors.

title: Coca-Cola, Molson Coors To Launch Simply-branded Alcoholic Drinks
summary: Coca-Cola and Molson Coors are expanding their partnership to launch Simply-branded alcoholic drinks in the US, following the success of their Topo Chico Hard Seltzer. This move reflects a growing trend of soft-drink makers entering the alcohol market. The new "Simply Spiked Lemonade" line will feature popular Simply juice flavors and aims to disrupt the full-flavor alcohol segment.

title: ESG Risk Management Makes Sense, but ESG Impact Is Less Straightforward
summary: This article distinguishes between ESG risk management and ESG impact, arguing that while managing ESG risks directly affects valuation, measuring and achieving positive ESG impact is far more complex and less directly tied to financial returns. It highlights challenges companies like Unilever face when prioritizing sustainability impact at the expense of core business fundamentals, and discusses the difficulty in objectively measuring the benefits of impact spending and aligning diverse investor values.

title: Large Birmingham manufacturer names new president, CEO
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Co. United, a large manufacturing leader based in Birmingham, has announced Mike Suco as its new president and CEO. Suco previously served as the company's senior vice president and chief commercial officer.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Streamlining Supply Chain, Boosting Ad Spend
summary: Colgate-Palmolive is implementing a global productivity program to streamline its supply chain and operations, anticipating significant pre-tax savings. The company is also increasing advertising spend across key categories like oral care and pet nutrition and investing in capacity to sustain volume growth amid price increases. Additionally, Colgate is launching a predictive tool for dentists to support its teeth-whitening product.

title: The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company, a strategic partner of the Ellen MacArthur Foundation, is committed to circular economy principles with a focus on sustainable packaging and a regenerative food system. They aim to have 25% of beverages sold through reuse models by 2030 and have implemented innovations like the "universal bottle" to scale returnable packaging across various markets. The company also links ESG performance, including diversity and inclusion, to executive incentives.

title: Beer Summit Takeaways: A-B CEO Previews Bud Light Next; Digital Marketing Opportunities on Facebook, Instagram; Lots of Seltzer Talk
summary: The article summarizes key discussions from Beer Business Daily’s Beer Industry Summit, detailing Anheuser-Busch InBev's CEO Brendan Whitworth's insights on Bud Light Next and e-commerce, Meta's Pablo Merheb's presentation on digital marketing for alcohol brands, and growth updates from Diageo’s Lone River Ranch Water, Molson Coors' Topo Chico Hard Seltzer, and Gopuff's expansion into beverage alcohol delivery. Constellation Brands CEO Bill Newlands also provided updates on the company’s Mexican import portfolio and Fresca Mixed.

title: Coca-Cola HBC ranked Europe’s most sustainable Beverage Company
summary: Coca-Cola HBC has been recognized as Europe's most sustainable beverage company for the 11th consecutive year, ranking among the top three globally according to S&P Global’s Annual Yearbook and the Dow Jones Sustainability Index. CEO Zoran Bogdanovic emphasized the company's long-standing commitment to sustainability and its goal to achieve net-zero emissions across its value chain by 2040. The company highlighted achievements such as significant CO2e and water savings, ethical sourcing, community programs, gender diversity in management, and sustainable packaging initiatives.

title: Urgent Coca-Cola Recall: If You Have Any Of These Sodas Or Juices, Throw Them Out
summary: Coca-Cola has issued two separate recalls for Minute Maid, Sprite, and Coca-Cola products due to potential foreign substances like metal. Consumers are advised to check date codes and batch numbers for affected Berry Punch, Strawberry Lemonade, Fruit Punch, Coca-Cola 12oz cans, and Sprite 12oz cans. The recalled products were sold in multiple states, and buyers should stop consumption immediately and seek a refund or discard the items.

title: Super Bowl Regional Ads Roundup: Busch Light, Sam Adams and Monday.com
summary: This article compiles a list of regional Super Bowl ads from various brands, highlighting their strategies for reaching targeted local markets rather than national audiences. It details campaigns from companies like Busch Light, Sam Adams, Monday.com, Novant Health, Michelob Ultra Pure Gold, and others, explaining how they leverage regional advertising to maximize impact and efficiency during the costly Super Bowl broadcast. The ads highlighted cover a range of industries from beverages and food to healthcare, tech, and insurance.

title: PepsiCo to launch hemp seed-infused drink under Rockstar Energy
summary: PepsiCo is launching a new hemp seed-infused drink called Rockstar Unplugged under its Rockstar Energy brand, aiming to attract younger, female consumers to the energy drink market. This new beverage contains significantly less caffeine than other Rockstar products and is infused with hemp seed oil, spearmint, and lemon balm, designed for relaxation. Unlike CBD-infused products which face legal restrictions, hemp seed-infused drinks are not banned in the U.S., though they are new territory for the market.

title: Folgers tunes in classic rock to try to perk up brand
summary: Folgers has launched a new campaign, replacing its long-standing "The Best Part of Wakin' Up" jingle with Joan Jett and the Blackhearts' "Bad Reputation." This effort aims to rebrand Folgers, traditionally seen as "grandma's coffee," for a younger audience interested in premium home-brew coffee, acknowledging changing consumer habits since the pandemic. The campaign will span various media, include experiential activations, and highlight Folgers' connection to New Orleans, mirroring similar recent brand updates by the parent company, J.M. Smucker Co., to connect with younger generations.

title: Country’s largest Coca-Cola bottler acquires distribution rights from Washington company
summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the U.S., has acquired the distribution rights for certain beverages from Coca-Cola Bottling Company Washington, N.C., Inc. This acquisition, effective January 1, 2022, includes trademark brands from The Coca-Cola Company, Monster Energy, BODYARMOR, and some Dr. Pepper products. The Washington Coca-Cola company, which has been family-owned since 1956, expressed honor in Coke Consolidated continuing its legacy of service.

title: Country's largest Coca-Cola bottler acquires distribution rights from Washington company
summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the U.S., has purchased the distribution rights for several beverages from Coca-Cola Bottling Company Washington, N.C. This acquisition, effective January 1, 2022, includes brands from The Coca-Cola Company, Monster Energy, BODYARMOR, and Dr. Pepper products. Both companies expressed enthusiasm for continuing a legacy of service in the Washington community, with the consolidated entity now marketing, promoting, and selling these beverages.

title: Hershey beats profits forecast after raising prices and strong holiday demand
summary: The Hershey Company exceeded its quarterly profit forecasts for the quarter ending December 2021, reporting revenues of $2.33 billion due to strong holiday demand and increased prices for its products. The company also anticipates an annual adjusted profit of $7.84 to $7.98 per share for 2022. Despite challenges like rising material costs and Omicron-related absenteeism, Hershey is confident in its strategic pricing and ability to adapt.

title: Mujer del día: Ana Botín, presidenta de Banco Santander
summary: Ana Botín, Presidenta de Banco Santander, lideró la entidad a un beneficio atribuido de 8.124 millones de euros en 2021, revirtiendo las pérdidas del año anterior. Santander planea distribuir el 40% del beneficio ordinario de 2022 en dividendos y recompra de acciones, reflejando su compromiso con la retribución al accionista. Botín ha estado al frente de la transformación cultural, comercial y tecnológica del Grupo Santander desde 2014, buscando impulsar la confianza y fidelidad de los clientes.

title: Michael Suco named new head of Coca-Cola United
summary: Michael Suco has been named the next president and CEO of Coca-Cola Bottling Company United Inc., effective August 1. Suco, currently senior vice president and chief commercial officer, has been with Coca-Cola for over 26 years and will be the eighth CEO in the company's 120-year history. He succeeds John Sherman, who is retiring but will remain on the board.

title: WPP gains early access to Instacart ad products in latest retail media bet
summary: WPP has partnered with Instacart, giving its clients early access to Instacart's new ad formats and analytics tools. This collaboration positions WPP as Instacart's first Analytics API partner, allowing for in-depth data integration and the co-development of an Instacart Ads agency certification program. The move highlights WPP's strategic focus on retail media, leveraging the boom in e-commerce and the increasing demand for effective advertising as third-party tracking methods decline.

title: NAPA Upgrades Its Know How, Adding New Agencies And Execs.
summary: NAPA Auto Parts has revamped its agency roster, appointing The Variable for brand strategy, creative, and social, Merkle for CRM, and Golin as its first public relations agency. These changes follow reviews initiated in October and are accompanied by promotions within NAPA's senior marketing team, including Jamie Walton to Executive VP, Chief Merchandising Officer, and Marti Walsh to VP, Marketing. The new partnerships aim to enhance NAPA's brand strategy, customer loyalty programs, and earned media engagement, with a new integrated creative campaign expected in the third quarter.

title: Beijing Olympics sponsor Procter & Gamble silent on Uyghur genocide after calling out US 'systemic racism'
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G), a sponsor of the 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing, is facing criticism for its silence on China's genocide of Uyghur Muslims. This silence contrasts sharply with the company's vocal stance on "systemic racism" in the U.S. P&G has reportedly downplayed its Olympics involvement and lobbied against legislation targeting corporate sponsors of the Games, prioritizing its significant revenue from the Chinese market.

title: Coca-Cola Consolidated acquires North Carolina distribution rights
summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc. has acquired distribution rights for various beverages in North Carolina from Coca-Cola Bottling Company Washington NC Inc. This includes trademark brands of The Coca-Cola Co. and its partners, such as Monster Energy Drinks, BodyArmor sports drinks, and certain Dr Pepper products.

title: Coca-Cola creates 3D designs in days with Substance 3D
summary: Coca-Cola is leveraging Adobe Substance 3D Stager to dramatically accelerate its design process, creating dozens of 3D designs in days instead of weeks, saving over $200,000 in photography costs, and completing 100% of creative in-house. This digital workflow, exemplified by the Topo Chico Hard Seltzer launch, enables faster iterations, more experimentation, and photorealistic renders, setting a new standard for their design and marketing efforts. The company aims to preserve its creative legacy while innovating for the future, with 3D design being crucial for their physical products in a digital world.

title: Americans Associate the Super Bowl with Pepsi and Budweiser
summary: A Morning Consult survey reveals that Pepsi is the brand most associated with the Super Bowl by 22% of U.S. adults, largely due to its sponsorship of the halftime show. Budweiser, a close second in brand association, is overwhelmingly considered to have the best Super Bowl commercials by 28% of respondents, highlighting its enduring advertising legacy despite not always airing ads. The survey also indicates that a significant portion of viewers pay close attention to Super Bowl ads and the halftime show.

title: With caution, #breakfreefromplastic welcomes Coca-Cola’s 25% Reusable Target By 2030
summary: The #breakfreefromplastic movement has cautiously welcomed Coca-Cola's announcement to sell 25% of all beverages globally in refillable/returnable containers by 2030. While seen as a step in the right direction, the environmental groups express skepticism due to Coca-Cola's past record as a top plastic polluter and urge for more aggressive targets and transparency. The movement also highlights the broader call for a legally binding Global Plastics Treaty to address plastic pollution comprehensively.

title: Coca-Cola's away-from-home volumes rise above pre-pandemic levels
summary: Coca-Cola announced that its away-from-home volumes surpassed pre-pandemic levels in Q4 2021, contributing to a strong financial year with 17% net revenue growth to $38.7 billion.
