title: Indorama Ventures, Coca-Cola open PET recycling plant
summary: Indorama Ventures and Coca-Cola have opened PETValue Philippines, the country's first food-grade, bottle-to-bottle recycling facility in Cavite province. This plant, a partnership with Coca-Cola Beverages Philippines, will recycle approximately 2 billion used PET bottles annually and supports Coca-Cola's "World Without Waste" initiative. Indorama Ventures is also expanding its global recycling capacity to meet its 2025 and 2030 sustainability targets.

title: Big CPGs have not been making food and drink healthier, study finds
summary: A study by the Access to Nutrition Initiative (ATNI) found that the 11 largest food companies in the U.S. have made inadequate progress in making their products healthier, more affordable, and accessible, despite public commitments. The average score for companies in ATNI's 2022 U.S. Index was only 4.2 out of 10, indicating poor performance, with 70% of products being "less healthy." The report emphasizes the need for more concrete actions from these companies to align with national goals for improving public health and reducing diet-related diseases.

title: VMLY&R Bolsters Global Agency Leadership for Coca-Cola Company Business
summary: VMLY&R has announced key leadership appointments for its Coca-Cola Company business, promoting Stephanie DeCelles to global client lead and naming Chase Cornett as global chief strategy officer. Both will join the OpenX from WPP team, a bespoke agency servicing Coca-Cola, to drive strategic focus and breakthrough work for the global brand. These appointments highlight VMLY&R's commitment to strengthening its partnership with The Coca-Cola Company.

title: An activist investor has a garbage plan for Coca-Cola
summary: Activist investor Engine No. 1, known for its win against Exxon, is now targeting Coca-Cola with a plan to address plastic waste. The fund, which holds a small stake in Coca-Cola, suggests the beverage giant invest in or partner with a waste-management company, specifically mentioning Republic Services, to enhance recycling infrastructure and meet its 2030 recycling goals. This move aims to tackle Coca-Cola's significant plastic pollution footprint and push for greater corporate responsibility in environmental sustainability.

title: The Coca‑Cola Company in South Africa continues to offer consumers choice
summary: The Coca-Cola Company (TCCC) in South Africa continues to prioritize consumer choice by offering seven low-calorie/low-kilojoule carbonated cold drinks, despite a global portfolio refresh that included discontinuing TaB. This strategy, according to Silke Bucker, Senior Marketing Director, is consumer-centric, aiming to satisfy evolving consumer needs and provide diverse options, including new products like Coca-Cola No Sugar No Caffeine. TCCC's focus remains on listening to and responding to consumer demand to accelerate its transformation into a total beverage company.

title: FDA to Redefine ‘Healthy’ As Leading CPG Brands Fail to Deliver Better Food
summary: The FDA is updating its definition of 'healthy' for food labeling to better reflect modern nutritional science, focusing on limiting added sugars, sodium, and saturated fats, and requiring a minimum serving of beneficial ingredients. This move comes as major CPG brands have largely failed to make their products healthier, despite pledges, with recent research showing little progress from the largest food companies in the U.S. toward improving the nutritional quality of their offerings. The new guidelines aim to help consumers make more informed choices, particularly regarding highly processed foods.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa crece a doble digito en ingresos y utilidades
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa reported double-digit growth in both revenues and utilities during the third quarter of the year, driven by increased sales volume and price adjustments. The company's total revenues rose by 18.2% to 57,093 million pesos, and net utility increased by 27.9%. John Santa Maria, CEO of Coca-Cola FEMSA, highlighted the company's strong momentum and strategic progress.

title: UN’s Coke sponsorship leaves bad taste with environmentally conscious groups
summary: Coca-Cola's sponsorship of the COP27 U.N. climate summit has sparked outrage among environmental groups and activists, who accuse the company of "greenwash" due to its significant contribution to plastic pollution. Critics argue that corporate involvement, especially from major polluters, undermines the integrity of climate negotiations and provides a marketing platform rather than genuine commitment to environmental solutions. The controversy highlights broader concerns about corporate lobbying and influence at critical international climate conferences.

title: Coca-Cola raises full-year outlook as earnings beat expectations
summary: Coca-Cola (KO) raised its full-year outlook for adjusted earnings per share and organic revenue growth after beating Wall Street's expectations for its third-quarter earnings. The company's organic revenue grew 16%, driven by price hikes, while unit case volume rose 4%. Coca-Cola expects commodity prices to remain volatile and anticipates further price hikes and challenges from foreign currency in 2023, while also focusing on offering more affordable options to consumers.

title: Coke Sponsoring COP27 Is the Definition of ‘Greenwashing,’ Activists Say
summary: Activists are criticizing the United Nations' decision to accept Coca-Cola as a sponsor for COP27, labeling the partnership as "pure greenwash." They point to Coca-Cola's significant contribution to global plastic waste and its historical lobbying against environmental regulations, despite the company's claims of working towards emission reductions and plastic cleanup. Environmental groups argue that corporations deeply implicated in climate issues should not be allowed to sponsor critical climate summits.

title: Shrinkflation is boosting Coca-Cola’s bottom line
summary: Coca-Cola is leveraging "shrinkflation" by offering smaller product packs to appeal to budget-conscious consumers amidst rising inflation. This strategy contributed to a 10% year-over-year net revenue rise to $11.1 billion in Q3, with unit case volume growing by 4%. The company has raised its full-year organic revenue and adjusted earnings per share guidance, despite anticipating continued volatility in commodity prices and competitive pressures.

title: Coca-Cola lifts forecasts as demand keeps pace with pricier sodas
summary: Coca-Cola Co (KO.N) raised its annual forecasts after strong Q3 results, mirroring rival PepsiCo, as multiple price increases for its sodas did not deter consumer demand. Despite concerns about inflation's impact on consumer spending in some regions, the company plans to introduce smaller capacity bottles to stabilize prices, and beat analyst expectations for both revenue and profit.

title: Coca-Cola prioritizes offering more value to consumers: ‘We're not chasing the competitors. We're chasing the consumers and the retailers,’ says CEO
summary: Coca-Cola is focusing on delivering increased value to consumers by introducing products at more affordable price points, amid a challenging global economic environment. Chairman and CEO James Quincey emphasized that the company is "chasing the consumers and the retailers," rather than competitors, to drive growth. This strategy includes investments in sports drinks like BODYARMOR and Powerade, along with offering affordable options like smaller multi-packs to address consumer pressures.

title: Coca-Cola builds Metaverse marketing trove with TMELAND
summary: Coca-Cola has partnered with Tencent Music Entertainment's TMELAND, China's first virtual social music platform, to launch a metaverse zone for its Fan Festival. This initiative allows users to create avatars, shop, play games, and interact with celebrity avatars, targeting a Gen Z audience. The venture highlights the growing potential for brands to engage consumers through immersive digital experiences in China, following similar moves by Pepsi and Adidas Originals on TMELAND.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners has pulled its signature mixers range
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) has discontinued its Signature Mixers range in the UK, citing a strategy focused on prioritizing best-performing brands. CCEP aims to streamline its portfolio and concentrate on widely appealing "hero products" in the competitive soft drinks market.

title: Negocio de logística de FEMSA reporta un robusto tercer trimetre de 2022
summary: FEMSA's Logistics and Distribution division reported a robust third quarter in 2022, achieving 19,986 million pesos, a 70.3% growth over the same period last year. This growth was significantly boosted by Envoy Solutions' strong performance, an American diversified distribution company. The company's OXXO Gas business also had a solid quarter, with a 33.6% increase in quarterly revenues and a return to pre-pandemic mobility levels.

title: Femsa planea abrir más quioscos de Valora y lanzar una fintech B2B en Europa
summary: Mexican bottler and retailer Femsa plans to expand its Swiss kiosk operator Valora in Europe, opening new stores and affiliating independent businesses in Germany. Additionally, Femsa intends to launch a B2B fintech service in Europe. This move follows Femsa's acquisition of Valora and comes after its consumer-facing fintech Spin by Oxxo received a license in Mexico, aiming for 10 million users by 2023.

title: Flows Into Consumer Staples ETFs Rebound on Economic Uncertainty
summary: Investors are increasingly moving back into consumer staples ETFs, a defensive strategy during economic uncertainty. The Invesco S&P 500® Equal Weight Consumer Staples ETF (RHS) has seen significant net inflows, indicating a preference for equal-weighted approaches to mitigate company-specific risks that are common in market-cap weighted funds dominated by a few large companies. This shift reflects advisors' search for downside protection while still participating in market upside in the current economic climate.

title: Greens push to oust Coke from COP 27 sponsorship
summary: Two environmental groups, Just Zero and Beyond Plastics, are calling for the removal of Coca-Cola Co. as a sponsor from COP 27, arguing that the company's role as a major plastics polluter undermines the climate conference's goals. They assert that plastics have become "the new coal" in terms of environmental impact and accuse Coca-Cola of greenwashing its image through sponsorship while continuing to contribute significantly to plastic waste. Critics cite reports highlighting Coca-Cola as the world's top plastic polluter and its lobbyists' efforts against real recycling improvements.

title: The anti-ESG funds exploiting the US political divide
summary: The article discusses the rise of anti-ESG funds in the US, which are exploiting the political divide by offering investments that prioritize shareholder value over socially responsible agendas. These funds, such as Strive Asset Management and ACVF, cater to investors who believe ESG investing is politically motivated and detrimental to financial returns. Despite their growing media attention, experts question their overall impact on corporate behavior and capital movement compared to traditional large asset managers.

title: Monster: Price Increases Tempering Costs
summary: Monster Beverage Company reported a 15.2% year-over-year sales growth in Q3, despite increased expenses and cost of goods impacting margins. The company implemented a 6% price increase in the U.S. and plans further international pricing actions to mitigate costs, while also defending its strategy of prioritizing product availability. Monster is focused on innovation with planned launches of Monster Energy Zero Sugar, its first alcoholic beverage "The Beast Unleashed," and Monster Tour Water, alongside an expanded alcoholic beverage pipeline and a new performance drink line, Rainstorm.

title: Coca-Cola plastic packaging up by 8.8% in one year
summary: Oceana reports that The Coca-Cola Company's plastic packaging increased by 8.8% in one year, amounting to over 579 million pounds. This increase occurred despite pledges to boost recycled content and decrease virgin plastic use, which the company failed to significantly advance. Oceana urges Coca-Cola to focus on increasing refillable bottle systems, which are more effective in reducing plastic pollution and carbon footprint than recycling efforts alone.

title: Why Apple raised the price of the iPhone, but not in the U.S. and China
summary: Apple increased the price of its iPhone 14 series for many international buyers due to the strong U.S. dollar and currency headwinds, which significantly impacted the company's revenue growth. CEO Tim Cook noted that foreign exchange headwinds were over 600 basis points last quarter, preventing double-digit revenue growth. While the U.S. and China avoided price hikes, consumers in markets like the U.K., Japan, Germany, and Australia saw significant increases, a strategy Apple previous reversed in 2019 due to declining sales, though they report no such drop-off this time.

title: Greece Fines Coca-Cola-Bottler Over Price-Fixing
summary: Greece has imposed a 10.34 million euro fine on Coca-Cola 3E, the largest bottler for The Coca Cola Company in the country, for price-fixing violations. The fine stems from a 2016 complaint alleging the bottler tried to block competitors in the soft drink market on Rhodes and the Dodecanese islands. This action occurs amidst global economic turbulence and increased scrutiny of corporate practices regarding price-fixing and abuses.

title: Wolverine Worldwide names Nicholas Long as lead independent director
summary: Wolverine World Wide, Inc. has appointed Nicholas T. Long as its lead independent director, effective November 4, 2022. Long, who has been a director since 2011 and chairs the compensation committee, succeeds Dr. David T. Kollat. CEO Brendan Hoffman highlighted Long's extensive experience in global brand-building and consumer-focused businesses as crucial for the company's strategic objectives.

title: B&B Theatres Signs 10-year Contract with The Coca-Cola Company
summary: B&B Theatres has announced a new 10-year partnership with The Coca-Cola Company, which will include the installment of Coca-Cola Freestyle machines across B&B's cinemas by holiday season 2022. This collaboration emphasizes shared values, an enhanced guest experience, and a mutual passion for cinema innovation. B&B Theatres is ranked #6 on Boxoffice PRO’s Giants of Exhibition 2022 list, operating 513 screens at 56 locations.

title: Coke Is a Sponsor of the Climate Summit in Egypt. Some Activists Aren’t Happy. (Published 2022)
summary: Coca-Cola's sponsorship of the COP27 climate summit in Egypt has drawn strong criticism from climate activists, who point to the company's increasing plastic production as detailed in a recent report. Activists argue that Coca-Cola, named the world's leading plastic polluter in 2021, is greenwashing its image while its plastic use, largely derived from fossil fuels, continues to rise. Despite Coca-Cola's claims of environmental commitments, a report from the Ellen MacArthur Foundation indicates that the company will likely miss its target for recyclable or compostable packaging by 2025.

title: Coca-Cola to restructure North American workforce with voluntary buyouts
summary: Coca-Cola is implementing a "voluntary separation program" including employee buyouts to restructure its North American workforce of approximately 6,000 people. This move follows previous restructurings and job cuts aimed at streamlining operations and focusing on growing brands, though the company states this current initiative is not primarily for cost-cutting. Employees have a short window, November 14-18, to decide on accepting the buyout offer.

title: Coca-Cola Supplies Alcorn Athletics with Gift
summary: Coca-Cola has gifted Alcorn State University Athletics with a new, fully-branded 35-foot equipment truck, capable of carrying over 6,000 pounds of gear. This donation is the result of a partnership between Alcorn President Dr. Felecia Nave and Coca-Cola representatives Russ Hendley and Mario Lee, providing a mobile billboard and essential transport for the Braves. The truck was presented on November 9, 2022, outside Jack Spinks – Marino Casem Stadium, and also came filled with Coca-Cola beverages.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper invests $50M in Athletic Brewing
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper has invested $50 million in Athletic Brewing, a nonalcoholic craft beer maker, acquiring a minority stake and a board seat. This investment is part of Athletic Brewing's $75 million fundraising round and reflects Keurig Dr Pepper's strategy to expand into the rapidly growing nonalcoholic beverage category. The move contrasts with competitors who are entering the ready-to-drink alcoholic beverage market.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper CEO pushed out after 3 months over personal conduct ‘violations’
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper CEO Ozan Dokmecioglu resigned after less than four months in the role due to unspecified violations of the company's Code of Conduct related to personal behavior, not strategy or financial reporting. Former CEO Bob Gamgort will return to the top position. The company emphasized its commitment to ethics and integrity for all employees.

title: How Droughts in Mexico Could Shape the Future of the Beer Industry (Published 2022)
summary: Mexico's severe droughts are intensifying the conflict between major beer corporations and local communities over water access. While brewers like Heineken continue to consume vast quantities of water, residents face shortages and health issues, sparking protests and a national debate on resource allocation. This situation is forcing the government and industry to confront the growing disparity in water access amid climate change, putting pressure on major global brands.

title: It’s not just Coca-Cola: Corporations have co-opted the UN climate talks
summary: This article criticizes the growing corporate influence at UN climate talks, specifically highlighting Coca-Cola's sponsorship of COP27 given its status as the world's largest plastic producer. Despite widespread criticism and a petition signed by nearly 240,000 people, corporations like Coca-Cola, Microsoft, IBM, and Bloomberg Philanthropies continue to play significant roles in these conferences. The piece suggests that this corporate involvement undermines the environmental goals of the climate talks.

title: COP27 Sponsor The Coca-Cola Company named worst plastic polluter for five years in a row according to 2022 Brand Audit
summary: A 2022 Brand Audit by Break Free From Plastic identified The Coca-Cola Company, PepsiCo, and Nestlé as the top plastic polluters for the fifth consecutive year, with Coca-Cola branded items outnumbering the next two polluters combined. Activists are commemorating a "Trashiversary" through global actions, calling for a legally binding Global Plastics Treaty to enforce waste reduction and corporate accountability, especially as voluntary commitments have failed to curb plastic use. The report highlights the irony of Coca-Cola sponsoring COP27, given that plastic relies heavily on fossil fuels, further fueling calls for systemic change towards reuse and alternatives.

title: Coca-Cola Seeing 'Encouraging Results' From Alcoholic Beverages Launches
summary: The Coca-Cola Company is reporting encouraging early results from its alcoholic beverage partnerships with Molson Coors and Constellation Brands for Simply Spiked Lemonade and Fresca Mixed. This follows their initial foray into the ready-to-drink alcoholic market with Lemon-Dou in 2018 in Japan. These initiatives support Coca-Cola's strategy to become a "total beverage company" with options for all occasions and need states.

title: Kraft Heinz Bets (Even) Bigger On Supply Chain Visibility
summary: Kraft Heinz is deepening its partnership with Microsoft, adopting the new Supply Chain Center to enhance supply chain visibility through AI-backed capabilities. This initiative is part of a larger transformation to integrate and centralize data, allowing for more agile risk assessment and improved product delivery across North America. The platform leverages AI models for demand and supply insights, order management automation, and Teams integration to streamline operations and decision-making.

title: COP27 Sponsor The Coca-Cola Company named worst plastic polluter for five years in a row according to 2022 Brand Audit
summary: The Coca-Cola Company, PepsiCo, and Nestlé have been identified as the world's top plastic polluters for the fifth consecutive year, according to the 2022 Brand Audit by Break Free From Plastic. This report highlights the ineffectiveness of corporate voluntary commitments in reducing environmental impact, with plastic packaging use actually increasing for many companies. Activists are advocating for a legally-binding Global Plastics Treaty to enforce reductions in plastic production and promote reuse-based alternatives, especially as Coca-Cola sponsors COP27 despite its significant plastic footprint.

title: Break Free From Plastic names Coca-Cola the world’s worst plastic polluter for fifth consecutive year
summary: For the fifth consecutive year, Break Free From Plastic has identified Coca-Cola as the world’s worst plastic polluter through its global brand audit report. Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Nestlé consistently rank as top polluters, highlighting that voluntary corporate commitments are insufficient to reduce environmental footprints. Activists are advocating for a legally binding Global Plastics Treaty to significantly cut plastic production, hold corporations accountable, and promote reuse models for packaging.

title: Coca-Cola Co.’s Mojo Kombucha shuts factory, warns products to disappear from shelves
summary: Coca-Cola Co.'s Mojo Beverages brand, known for Mojo Kombucha, is closing its kombucha factory. As a result, its products will no longer be available on shelves in the near future. The company stated this was a difficult decision.

title: Molson Coors to End La Colombe, HEXO Partnerships
summary: Molson Coors announced it is ending its partnerships with coffee roaster La Colombe and cannabis producer Hexo Corp. Effective March 31, 2023, the La Colombe partnership will conclude due to logistical challenges for distributors, while the Truss CBD beverage joint venture with Hexo will dissolve at the end of 2022 due to regulatory hurdles. Molson Coors plans to reallocate resources to other non-beer ventures like ZOA energy drink and Topo Chico Spirited.

title: Coca Cola Christmas Truck confirms its return for 2022
summary: Coca-Cola has confirmed the return of its Christmas Truck Tour for 2022, featuring a winter market theme and supporting FareShare by donating up to 100,000 meals to those in need. The tour will offer interactive activities, personalized Coca-Cola products, and will see the beloved "Holidays Are Coming" advert return to TV. For the first time, Coca-Cola is also collaborating with RNIB and NaviLens to make its packaging accessible for blind and partially sighted people.

title: Popular Coca-Cola Christmas Truck tour returns for 2022
summary: The Coca-Cola Christmas Truck tour is returning for 2022, featuring a Christmas market theme, interactive activities, and food huts. This year, the tour supports FareShare, a charity fighting hunger and food waste, with Coca-Cola donating the equivalent of one meal for every attendee. The company is also collaborating with RNIB to implement NaviLens technology on promotional multipacks, making packaging accessible for blind and partially sighted people.

title: Coca-Cola Rethinks Hybrid Work to Tell a Better Workplace Story
summary: Coca-Cola is rethinking its hybrid work strategy to create a more compelling workplace story for its employees, focusing on connection, social capital, and flexible office design. This initiative, highlighted at the CoreNet Global Summit, involved redesigning their Singapore headquarters to reflect local culture and provide varied work areas to support hybrid work. The article emphasizes that a successful hybrid model requires more than just technology, integrating aesthetic design, amenities, and HR policies to enhance the employee experience and attract workers back to the office.

title: Cabarrus County joins Concord in approving more incentives for Red Bull, Rauch at $1B-plus beverage hub
summary: Cabarrus County has approved additional incentives for Red Bull and Rauch North America, who, along with Ball Corp., plan a an expanded $1 billion-plus beverage hub at The Grounds at Concord. This move follows Concord's earlier consideration of incentives for increased investment in the project. The companies are set to break ground on the facility next year.

title: Coca-Cola will now make local deliveries in Belgium with 30 electric Renault Trucks vehicles
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) is deploying 30 electric Renault Trucks vehicles for "last mile" deliveries in Belgium, starting with five in the Antwerp area. This initiative, part of a €7 million investment, aims to electrify one-fifth of CCEP's Belgian fleet, reduce CO2 emissions by 75% compared to diesel trucks, and contribute to the company's goal of cutting overall CO2 emissions by 30% by 2030 and achieving climate neutrality by 2040. The trucks will cover average routes of 150 km per day, charged overnight with 100% green energy.

title: LG Household & Health Care appoints first female CEO
summary: LG Household & Health Care has appointed Lee Jung-ae as its first female CEO, effective December 1. Lee, a veteran marketer, has a strong background in the company's cosmetics, beverage, and household goods divisions. This appointment is part of broader personnel changes across LG affiliates, including new CEOs for LG CNS and promotions within LG Electronics and LG Chem.

title: Meet The Markets: Introducing Spain
summary: This article introduces Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) in Spain, highlighting its history, economic contribution, and commitment to sustainability and community programs. It details CCEP Spain's innovation in product offerings, significant job creation, and environmental efforts like emissions reduction, plastic recycling, and waste collection. Key facts and figures demonstrate CCEP's substantial presence and impact on the Spanish economy and environment.

title: Coca-Cola Femsa aumenta los precios de refrescos, agua y leche
summary: Coca-Cola Femsa announced a third price increase for its products, including soft drinks, water, and milk, effective November 28th. The price hike, ranging from 1 to 2 pesos, is attributed to rising raw material costs and inflation. Specific price adjustments are detailed for various Coca-Cola, flavored soft drinks, Santa Clara milk, Ades products, and Ciel water presentations.

title: What Can Brands Learn from Coca-Cola’s Greenwashing Lawsuit Win?
summary: Coca-Cola successfully defended itself against a greenwashing lawsuit filed by Earth Island Institute, which accused the company of false advertising regarding its sustainability claims. The court dismissed the case primarily because Coca-Cola's statements were deemed aspirational, not actionable, and not directly tied to product labeling. This ruling suggests a potential challenge for future greenwashing claims against companies, especially regarding general corporate ethos statements.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Names Henrique Braun to Newly Created Role of President, International Development
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced the creation of a new role, President, International Development, and named Henrique Braun to fill it, effective January 1, 2023. Braun will oversee seven operating units, including Latin America, Japan and South Korea, Africa, and others. John Murphy, President and CFO, will also take on oversight of the Bottling Investments Group.

title: Coca-Cola creates new role of president, International Development
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Henrique Braun to the newly created role of President, International Development, effective January 1, 2023. Braun will oversee seven operating units covering dozens of countries and territories, reporting directly to CEO James Quincey. This new role expands his responsibilities beyond his current position as president of the Latin America operating unit, which he has held since 2020.

title: Coke’s sustainably chief throws down a marker on regulations for reporting supplier emissions
summary: Coca-Cola's chief sustainability officer, Bea Perez, announced the company's support for the SEC's proposed regulations on supplier emissions, or Scope 3 emissions, despite previous quibbles regarding implementation details for smaller suppliers. Perez emphasized the need for fairness and consistency in reporting, while Kristina Wyatt, formerly of the SEC, clarified that the proposed rules allow for flexibility, including using industry benchmarks for smaller entities during a phase-in period. The article highlights Coca-Cola's existing voluntary climate targets to reduce total greenhouse gas emissions by 25% by 2030 and its ambition for net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.

title: Coca-Cola announces Christmas truck is coming to Bristol
summary: Coca-Cola's famous Christmas truck is returning to Cribbs Causeway in Bristol on December 3rd as part of its 'Magic of Giving’ Christmas campaign. This year, the event will feature a winter market, festive food, and interactive games, with Coca-Cola donating the equivalent of a meal to FareShare for every visitor. The initiative aims to support FareShare's efforts in tackling food poverty, with a goal of funding 200,000 meals.

title: How Coca-Cola’s new marketing leader will approach the job
summary: Shakir Moin has been promoted to lead Coca-Cola Co.'s North American marketing. Moin previously headed the company’s Costa coffee business and is known for working in Costa stores to gain business insights. The article will detail his approach to his new role.

title: Coca-Cola's Plastic Pollution Problem
summary: The Sierra Club criticizes Coca-Cola for its significant plastic pollution, highlighting the company's annual production of 3 million tons of plastic packaging and its alleged misleading recycling claims. The article discusses Coca-Cola's history of prioritizing plastic over more recyclable materials like aluminum and details a lawsuit filed by the Sierra Club against Coca-Cola regarding false advertising of its bottles' recyclability.

title: John Murphy to Become President and Chief Financial Officer of The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced that John Murphy will become President and Chief Financial Officer, effective October 1. Murphy will add the president role following the retirement of Brian Smith, who served as president and chief operating officer since 2019. This change will expand Murphy's duties to include oversight of Global Ventures, Platform Services, O2O digital transformation, and customer and commercial leadership.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners Australia inaugurates US$43.7m Moorabbin can line
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) Australia has opened a new US$43.7 million can line at its Moorabbin site in Victoria, designed to meet rising consumer demand for canned beverages and increase local production. The facility is CCEP Australia's most sustainable production line, boasting significant water and energy efficiencies, including a yearly saving equivalent to six Olympic-sized swimming pools of water. The new line can produce up to 1700 cans per minute and, alongside a new distribution center in Mentone, is expected to reduce inter-state freight and carbon emissions.

title: The Coca-Cola Company names Henrique Braun as president, international development
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Henrique Braun as president of international development, a new role overseeing seven operating units across many countries. Braun, who previously led the Latin America operating unit, will begin his new duties on January 1, 2023, reporting to CEO James Quincey. John Murphy, president and CFO, will also take on oversight of the company’s Bottling Investments Group.

title: Executives from eBay and Golden State Foods Join GS1 US Board of Governors
summary: GS1 US has elected Scott Gaffney from eBay and Brian Dick from Golden State Foods to its Board of Governors. These industry leaders will help guide GS1 US's strategy to enhance supply chain efficiency and visibility across various sectors, supporting members with digital transformation and demand planning. Their expertise is expected to be instrumental in optimizing supply chains to meet consumer needs.

title: Layoffs in food industry mount as PepsiCo joins Coca-Cola, General Mills, Walmart and others in cost-savings and restructuring efforts
summary: Major food industry players like PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, and General Mills are implementing layoffs and restructuring efforts to combat inflationary pressures and manage rising commodity costs. This trend extends to food tech companies, foodservice providers, and retailers like Walmart and Amazon, all seeking cost savings. Despite these workforce reductions, the consumer packaged goods industry still faces a significant number of job openings, indicating a complex labor market influenced by increased wage demands.

title: PepsiCo sets global packaging goals following shareholder scrutiny
summary: PepsiCo has set an ambitious global packaging goal for 2030, aiming to deliver up to 20% of its beverage servings through reusable models, doubling its current rate. This move is part of the PepsiCo Positive (pep+) sustainability programme and is accelerated by shareholder pressure, particularly from "As You Sow." The company plans to expand its SodaStream business and work with bottlers to increase reusable plastic and glass bottle offerings to achieve this target.

title: Kraft Heinz Co. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) stock advanced 1.19% on Wednesday, closing at $39.89, despite a generally grim trading session for the broader stock market. The company's stock outperformed competitors like Coca-Cola Co. (KO), PepsiCo Inc. (PEP), and Mondelez International Inc. Cl A (MDLZ) and ended a two-day losing streak. The stock is currently $4.98 below its 52-week high, reached on May 10th.

title: Say We Care Programme
summary: The Coca-Cola Foundation is funding the 'Say We Care' initiative to provide essential relief packs to 6,000 vulnerable families across nine districts in Sri Lanka. This effort responds to the severe economic crisis and high food insecurity in the country. The initiative specifically targets pregnant mothers, children, persons with disabilities, and low-income households, building on TCCF's history of supporting communities during challenging times.

title: From Nostalgic to Cheeky: 12+ Christmas Commercials and What They Teach Us About Storytelling
summary: This article analyzes over 12 Christmas commercials, ranging from nostalgic classics to modern, cheeky campaigns, to extract lessons in effective storytelling for marketers. It explores how brands use emotion, creativity, and unique narratives to create memorable holiday advertisements that resonate with audiences. The piece highlights various storytelling takeaways, emphasizing the importance of relatable characters, emotional impact, and innovative approaches in holiday marketing.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper spends $863M for stake in C4 Energy maker
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper is acquiring a 30% stake in Nutrabolt, the maker of C4 Energy and Xtend Energy drinks, for $863 million. This deal includes a long-term sales and distribution agreement, giving Keurig Dr Pepper a significant entry into the rapidly growing performance energy drink market. The investment strategically positions Keurig Dr Pepper to adapt to changing consumer trends in the beverage industry.

title: Coke CMO Melanie Boulden Moves to Tyson Foods
summary: Melanie Boulden, formerly North America CMO for Coca-Cola, is moving to Tyson Foods as EVP, Chief Growth Officer, a newly created role, effective February 6. She will oversee global brand marketing, innovation, R&D, and communications for Tyson's portfolio. Boulden previously led Coca-Cola's Venturing & Emerging Brands unit and served as President, Still Beverages Business Unit, and her shift comes as Tyson Foods reported record sales despite flat or declining volumes in some segments.

title: People on the Move: Altria, Paytronix & PepsiCo Inc.
summary: This article details recent executive changes at several companies in the convenience store industry, including Altria Group Inc., Paytronix Systems Inc., and PepsiCo Inc. It highlights new board appointments, C-suite changes, and promotions aimed at driving growth, efficiency, and strategic initiatives within these organizations.

title: Former Coca-Cola Exec Melanie Boulden Joins Tyson as Chief Growth Officer
summary: Tyson Foods Inc. announced Melanie Boulden, former chief marketing officer at Coca-Cola North America, will join the company as its first chief growth officer. In her new role, Boulden will oversee brand marketing for Tyson Foods' diverse portfolio and is expected to start on February 8. CEO Donnie King highlighted her experience and the importance of this new role for driving future growth.

title: Coca-Cola United automates over 50,000 orders in complex SAP invoicing process with Microsoft Power Platform
summary: Coca-Cola United has significantly improved its operational efficiency by using Microsoft Power Platform to automate two key processes: on-demand shipment requests and a complex SAP invoicing process. The automation reduced order validation time from half a day to seconds and enabled the processing of over 50,000 orders, freeing up valuable employee time and supporting strategic growth. The company plans to continue automating more business processes using Microsoft Power Automate RPA capabilities, further reducing labor costs and improving accuracy.

title: CELSIUS Sparkling Lemon Lime
summary: CELSIUS has introduced a new Sparkling Lemon Lime flavor, marking the 30th flavor in its portfolio. The company launched this flavor to capitalize on the popularity of lemon and lime combinations in the sparkling beverage category. CELSIUS energy drinks are distinguished by being made with high-quality ingredients, seven essential vitamins, and zero sugar, positioning them as a healthier alternative to other energy drinks.

title: Port of Olympia Commission votes 3-0 to approve ground lease with Coca-Cola bottler
summary: The Port of Olympia Commission unanimously approved a long-term ground lease with Swire Coca-Cola for 95 acres near Olympia Regional Airport, despite public concerns about the pace of the deal and environmental impacts. The bottling company plans to build a facility that could employ up to 600 people, though specific job numbers and water usage details were not fully disclosed. This approval is an initial step, with further environmental assessments and city land-use approvals required.

title: Commission approves plans for new Coca-Cola plant in Olathe
summary: The Olathe Planning Commission has approved preliminary plans for a new 1 million-square-foot Coca-Cola bottling facility. Heartland Coca-Cola Bottling Company plans to build the facility in two phases, creating a significant amount of office, warehouse, and production space, along with extensive parking. Construction is anticipated to begin in April 2023, with the facility expected to open in August 2024, operating 24/7 with an estimated 150 employees per shift.

title: Los principales 4 proveedores de bebidas de J&J Snack Foods
summary: J&J Snack Foods Corp. relies on The Coca-Cola Company, Keurig Dr. Pepper, Pepsi Cola Company, and Jogue as its top four frozen beverage syrup suppliers. The company is a major producer of soft pretzels in the U.S., manufactures snacks, and distributes frozen beverages to food service and retail supermarket sectors. Soft pretzels constituted 19% of the company's revenue in fiscal year 2022.

title: Coca-Cola , Madlib, and Mark Ronson create recycling music
summary: Coca-Cola has partnered with music producers Mark Ronson and Madlib to launch "Recycled Records," an initiative that transforms sounds from the plastic bottle recycling process into music. This campaign includes an original EP, a sound library for fans to remix, and a short film narrated by MC Lyte, aiming to highlight the company's transition to clear plastic packaging for Sprite, Fresca, and Seagram's to improve recyclability. The project underscores Coca-Cola's broader World Without Waste goals by creatively engaging consumers with the circular economy.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Partners with Musical Legends Mark Ronson and Madlib to Launch “Recycled Records”
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has partnered with musical legends Mark Ronson and Madlib to launch "Recycled Records," a campaign featuring an original EP and sound library created from the sounds of the bottle-to-bottle recycling process. This initiative celebrates Sprite, Fresca, and Seagram’s transition from green to clear plastic packaging, aiming to increase the availability of high-quality, food-grade recycled plastic. Fans can also interact with a digital beat machine to create their own compositions using the sounds, highlighting the connection between music sampling and the closed-loop recycling process.

title: How Coca-Cola turns to its Freestyle machine to create shelf-ready flavors
summary: Coca-Cola uses its Freestyle dispenser data as a "holy grail" for developing new product flavors for store shelves. The Freestyle machines, which pour over 11 million drinks daily across 50,000 locations, provide valuable real-time data on consumer preferences. This data has informed successful launches of new bottle and can flavors like Sprite Cherry and Coke with Orange Vanilla, demonstrating a methodical approach to innovation and a high likelihood of market success for these Freestyle-inspired beverages.

title: Last Call: Judge Sends Beer Definition Lawsuit to Trial; Ontario Craft Brewery M&A On Fire; Molson Coors Discontinues Sharp’s, Coors Pure
summary: A federal judge has sent a lawsuit regarding the definition of beer between Grupo Modelo and Constellation Brands to trial, focusing on whether hard seltzers fall under their licensing agreement. Concurrently, the Canadian craft beer market is active with Carlsberg acquiring Waterloo Brewing for C$144 million, and SymBev Inc. acquiring three Ontario breweries. Meanwhile, Molson Coors is discontinuing its Sharp’s non-alcoholic and Coors Pure brands due to underperformance.

title: Coca-Cola Business Model
summary: This article details the Coca-Cola business model, outlining its historical development, revenue streams, customer segments, value propositions, and operational aspects. It also includes a comprehensive SWOT analysis, examining the company's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats in the global beverage industry. The analysis highlights Coca-Cola's strong brand, global reach, and diversified product portfolio as key strengths, while addressing challenges like reliance on sugary drinks, environmental impact, and increasing competition.

title: WPP invests in new Atlanta Campus
summary: WPP is establishing a new Campus in Atlanta's Old Fourth Ward, bringing together over 400 employees from ten of its agencies into a single, world-class workspace. This development is part of the largest mixed-use project on the Atlanta BeltLine and is designed to foster greater collaboration among WPP agencies and with clients, especially The Coca-Cola Company. The new campus, set to be completed in Q2 2023, will be WPP's sixth in North America and aims for a "Gold" LEED rating.

title: Supplier Spotlights: The Coca-Cola Co., Harbor Wholesale & Old Trapper
summary: This article highlights recent initiatives and acquisitions by various convenience store suppliers. Key developments include AMCON Distributing Co.'s acquisition of Henry's Foods Inc., Blackhawk Network surpassing 1 billion rebate transactions, and The Coca-Cola Co.'s "Recycled Records" campaign promoting bottle-to-bottle recycling. Additionally, The Ferrero Group is set to acquire Wells Enterprises, Harbor Wholesale acquired MTC Distributing Co., NielsenIQ launched Omnisales data for emerging brands, Old Trapper sponsored college basketball tournaments, and PepsiCo unveiled its digital Holiday Village while also doubling its packaging goal for reusable beverage servings.

title: Kellogg divests Russian operations to local snacks maker Chernogolovka
summary: Kellogg Co announced its decision to divest its Russian operations to local snacks and drinks maker Chernogolovka, joining other Western brands leaving the country. This move follows Kellogg's earlier suspension of product imports and investments in Russia due to the Ukraine invasion. Chernogolovka, known for snacks and beverages, has also stepped in to supply soft drinks to Russian fast-food outlets after major soda companies halted sales.

title: What if New Coke Had Been a Government Program?
summary: Art Carden uses the examples of failed commercial products like New Coke, Crystal Pepsi, and McDonald's menu items to illustrate the efficiency of market economies over government programs. He argues that market feedback mechanisms like profits and losses quickly correct mistakes, unlike government initiatives which lack such disciplinary forces and can perpetuate inefficient resource allocation. The article suggests that consumer choice, even in seemingly excessive forms like numerous chicken sandwich options, ultimately leads to better outcomes than centralized top-down decisions.

title: Peter Sealey, Former Marketing Executive at Coca-Cola and Columbia Pictures, Dies At 82
summary: Peter Sealey, former global chief marketing officer of The Coca-Cola Company and a key figure in marketing for Columbia Pictures during the 1980s, has died at 82 due to complications after a fall. Sealey oversaw successful campaigns like "Always Coca-Cola" and contributed to the marketing of iconic films such as "Ghostbusters" and "The Karate Kid." After leaving Coca-Cola in 1993, he became a global speaker, consultant, and professor, and was also known for his philanthropic efforts.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper grows as company, gains on competition
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper, America's third-largest soft drink maker, is growing and gaining market share despite the overall decline in soda consumption. The company increased its dollar share by 9% from 2003 to 2021, now holding 25% of the U.S. retail market, behind Coca-Cola (40%) and Pepsi (29%). This growth highlights Keurig Dr Pepper's success in a competitive beverage industry.

title: Warren Buffett Surpassed Jeff Bezos in Wealth, May Overtake Bill Gates
summary: Warren Buffett has surpassed Jeff Bezos in wealth this year and is nearing Bill Gates' net worth, potentially making him the second-richest American after Elon Musk. This shift is attributed to the strong performance of Berkshire Hathaway stock compared to the declines seen in tech giants like Amazon, Microsoft, and Tesla. Despite significant charitable donations, Buffett's conservative investment strategy has proven resilient in the current economic climate, attracting investors away from growth stocks.

title: Sanford Coca-Cola, American Gifts buildings sold
summary: A Charlotte-based commercial real estate firm, Beacon Partners, acquired two significant distribution sites in Sanford, NC, during the final quarter of 2022. One purchase involved the Coca-Cola Bottling Company's facility on Hawkins Avenue for $3.374 million, which Coca-Cola plans to vacate in 2023 for a new Chatham County operation. The other acquisition was a 100,000-square-foot facility on Rex McLeod Drive for $4.34 million, currently leased by American Gifts, which will continue to rent from the new owners.

title: Why Coca-Cola is getting dragged on the internet
summary: Coca-Cola is facing online backlash after an entrepreneur alleged the company paid civil rights groups to oppose soda taxes and food stamp restrictions. This social media controversy, amplified by investor Bill Ackman, highlights a growing narrative around the health impacts of sugary drinks and raises questions about potential policy implications and corporate accountability. The article also touches on Senator Debbie Stabenow's upcoming retirement and the FDA's inaction regarding heavy metals in baby food.

title: 2023 Bottler of the Year: Heartland Coca-Cola Bottling Co.
summary: Heartland Coca-Cola Bottling Co. has been named Beverage Industry's 2023 Bottler of the Year for its strong community ties, commitment to team members, and significant growth since its refranchising in 2017. The company, led by Ulysses "Junior" Bridgeman and Chuck Wyant, emphasizes family, community, inclusion, and service, investing in local neighborhoods and supporting organizations like the Veterans Community Project. Heartland plans a major expansion with a new 600,000-square-foot production campus in Olathe, Kansas, set to be fully operational by 2025, while continuing to innovate with sparkling and zero-sugar beverages and addressing industry challenges like the CDL driver shortage.

title: Coke, PepsiCo Are Target of Probe by Federal Trade Commission
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has initiated a preliminary probe into the pricing practices of Coca-Cola Co. and PepsiCo Inc. in the U.S. beverage market. The investigation focuses on potential violations of a law prohibiting suppliers from offering preferential prices to certain customers or those in specific regions. This comes as Coke holds 43% and PepsiCo 23% of U.S. soda sales volume.

title: Pepsi, Coke soda pricing targeted in new federal probe
summary: The Federal Trade Commission has launched a preliminary investigation into Coca-Cola and PepsiCo's pricing strategies for potential price discrimination in the soft drink market. This probe revives the largely dormant Robinson-Patman Act of 1936, which prohibits suppliers from offering better prices to large retailers over smaller competitors. The investigation signals the Biden administration's broader effort to apply antitrust scrutiny beyond the tech sector to traditional large companies.

title: BCI es la empresa con mejor reputación de Chile
summary: BCI has been recognized as the company with the best reputation in Chile for the eighth consecutive year, according to the Merco Chile 2022 ranking. Banco de Chile maintained its second position, while Mercado Libre rose to third place. Adicionalmente, Andrónico Luksic of Grupo Luksic was named the business leader with the best reputation for the fourth consecutive year.

title: Pepsi is ditching Sierra Mist for a new Sprite rival
summary: Pepsi is replacing its Sierra Mist soda with a new lemon-lime brand called Starry, aiming to better compete with Coca-Cola's Sprite. Starry is caffeine-free, features "higher citrus flavors," and is being marketed towards younger consumers with a Gen Z-appealing slogan. This move comes after Sierra Mist consistently failed to gain significant market share against Sprite over its 24-year history.

title: Federal report shows companies invested $15 billion in TN since 2021
summary: A federal report indicates that companies have invested approximately $15 billion in Tennessee since 2021, spurred by President Joe Biden's economic plan. Key investments include Ford's $5.5 billion near Memphis, Arconic's $100 million in East Tennessee, and Eastman Chemical's $250 million, alongside significant funding for electric vehicle battery manufacturing and infrastructure projects. The report highlights the revitalization of manufacturing, supply chain strengthening, and positive impacts on healthcare costs for Tennesseans.

title: 3 things investors can learn from Warren Buffett
summary: This article outlines three key investing lessons from Warren Buffett: avoiding overpayment for stocks and practicing patience, favoring companies with competitive advantages ("moats"), and opting for index funds when uncertain. It emphasizes researching investments, demanding a margin of safety, and holding long-term, while also highlighting the importance of identifying businesses with sustainable competitive advantages and the diversification benefits of low-cost index funds.

title: Report: FTC Opens Pricing Discrimination Probe Into Coke, Pepsi
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has initiated a preliminary investigation into Coca-Cola and PepsiCo for potential price discrimination within the soft drink market. This probe revives the dormant Robinson-Patman Act, which prohibits offering lower prices to larger retailers at the expense of smaller ones. While the investigation is in its early stages, it signals increased antitrust action under the Biden administration, despite concerns from critics that enforcing this law could lead to higher consumer prices.

title: Coca-Cola names new president in the Chinese market
summary: Coca-Cola has appointed Gilles Leclerc as the new president of Coca-Cola Greater China & Mongolia, marking the first leadership change in this key market since 2020. Leclerc, who previously led Coca-Cola's McDonald's Division, replaces Vamsi Mohan Thati. The Chinese market continues to be a crucial growth driver for the beverage giant, as highlighted by CEO James Quincy's comments on its resilient performance despite pandemic impacts.

title: Pepsi is ditching Sierra Mist for a new Sprite rival
summary: Pepsi is replacing its lemon-lime soda Sierra Mist with a new offering called "Starry" to better compete with Coca-Cola's Sprite. Starry is described as being fruitier and more aromatic than its predecessor and will be available in regular and sugar-free versions. Sierra Mist was on the market for 24 years but failed to significantly impact Sprite's sales.

title: Simply Mixology Raises the Bar of the At-Home Mocktail and Cocktail Experience
summary: Simply Mixology has launched a new line of fruit-forward, all-natural flavored juice beverages designed for creating both cocktails and mocktails at home. Available in Strawberry Guava Mojito, Lime Margarita, and Peach Sour, these products cater to growing consumer trends of at-home cocktail making and the rise of booze-free options. The brand, nearing its 21st anniversary and $2 billion in annual retail sales, aims to simplify and elevate at-home drinking experiences with these versatile mixers.

title: Kraft Heinz Co. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Shares of Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) fell 0.21% on Tuesday, underperforming the broader market and several competitors. This marked the stock's third consecutive day of losses, closing $2.54 below its 52-week high. Competitors such as Coca-Cola Co. (KO) and PepsiCo Inc. (PEP) saw gains.

title: Stock Analysis: Is Coca-Cola Company (KO) a good buy this year?
summary: The Coca-Cola Company (KO) has demonstrated resilience against market headwinds and macroeconomic uncertainties, maintaining stable sales and earnings. The stock is considered a safe growth option due to strong earnings, regular dividend increases (currently 2.8% yield), and innovative product strategies like healthier options. Analysts expect the company to continue its positive performance and anticipate Q4 earnings of $0.45 per share on revenues of $9.98 billion.

title: Monster plots affordable energy expansion to drive Asia growth
summary: Monster Beverage Corp is planning to expand its affordable Predator energy drink line into China as part of a strategy to emphasize the value segment in Asia. This move aims to differentiate Monster from competitors like Red Bull, which has sold a cheaper version of its flagship product in China through a local partner. The company intends to focus on the mainstream price points with Predator.

title: London Coca-cola factory emergency as 200 people evacuated amid 'chemical incident'
summary: A Coca-Cola factory in Sidcup, London, was temporarily evacuated after a hydrochloric acid spillage, leading to 200 people being cleared from the premises. Six fire engines and police responded to the incident on Cray Road, which was closed in both directions. Coca-Cola Europacific Partners confirmed the issue was resolved, with no risk to colleagues, and thanked emergency services for their swift response.

title: Monster: Crowded 2023 Innovation Slate Includes Tour Water, Clean Energy
summary: Monster Energy Company outlined its extensive 2023 innovation strategy, introducing new ventures into better-for-you energy, alcohol, and canned water categories. Key launches include Monster Zero Sugar, the malt beverage line The Beast Unleashed, and Tour Water, transitioning from an exclusive product to retail. The company also unveiled new "Clean Energy" line Reign Storm and various flavor extensions across its existing brands, while also noting positive outlooks for reduced manufacturing costs but potential challenges with the high volume of new products.

title: Strong Drinks Brand + Strong Regional Market = Bullish Gains Ahead
summary: Embotelladora Andina S.A. (NYSE: AKO.B), a primary distributor of Coca-Cola products in Latin America, is projected for "Strong Bullish" gains due to the significant growth in nonalcoholic beverage sales in the region. The company boasts strong financial performance, an impressive 94 out of 100 on the Stock Power Ratings system, and is expected to outperform the broader market by 3X within the next 12 months. Its strong quality, value, and momentum factors, combined with a 15.2% dividend, make it a compelling investment.

title: The COCA-COLA® Foundation to fund Clean Bhutan’s new recycling project in Thimphu
summary: The Coca-Cola Foundation is funding Clean Bhutan's "Druk Larzo Thimphu" project, a new recycling initiative in Thimphu, Bhutan. This project aims to raise awareness about waste segregation, improve disposal practices, and create job opportunities, especially for women and youth, through plastic waste recycling. The goal is to recycle 25,000 Kgs of plastic waste over 12 months and positively impact over 2,500 households.

title: Westrock Coffee’s investment in RTD, cold coffee beverages could help triple profit
summary: Westrock Coffee anticipates tripling its profitability within the next three years by expanding its flavors, extractions, and ingredients business and by completing a new production facility. These investments are driven by a significant shift in consumer preferences towards cold, ready-to-drink coffee and plant-based alternatives over traditional hot, dairy-based beverages. The new $300 million facility in Conway, Ark., will allow Westrock to meet growing demand and transition its business to higher-margin products, ultimately positioning it as a leading player in the RTD coffee market.

title: Vita Coco’s reinvention: How reassessing its customer base is paying off
summary: Vita Coco has seen significant sales and marketing growth after reassessing its core customer base, shifting focus from "yoga moms" to a younger, urban, and multicultural demographic. The company is exploring new consumption occasions, including alcohol mixers, and considering M&A opportunities in the healthy beverage space, while also carefully growing other brands in its portfolio like Runa and PWR LIFT. This strategic pivot has allowed Vita Coco to maintain profitability and market leadership despite past category slowdowns and exits by beverage giants.

title: JEPI Vs. SCHD: Which Dividend ETF Is The Better Buy
summary: This article compares two popular dividend ETFs, JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPI) and Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD), to determine which is a better investment. It highlights JEPI's monthly high-yield distribution versus SCHD's appeal as a "triple threat" for dividend investors. The author, a Certified Public Accountant, aims to provide insights for long-term financial freedom through undervalued dividend stocks and high-growth opportunities.

title: Responsible business
summary: Coca-Cola outlines its commitment to responsible business practices, focusing on environmental sustainability, water stewardship, and community investment. The company aims for 100% recyclable packaging by 2025 and 50% recycled material by 2030, alongside significant water replenishment efforts and agricultural ecosystem investments in India.

title: Package Deal: In 1915, Coca-Cola had many imitators. Then it designed a patented bottle nobody could copy.
summary: In 1915, facing numerous imitators, Coca-Cola launched a challenge to glass companies to design a bottle so distinctive it could be recognized by touch or when broken. The Root Glass Company's design, inspired by the cocoa bean, became the iconic Coca-Cola bottle introduced in 1916. This patented design not only foiled knock-offs but also became a classic in packaging history, influencing design beyond beverages, such as in "Coke bottle style" automobiles.

title: Berry, Coca-Cola implement tethered caps in EU markets
summary: Berry and Coca-Cola have collaborated to implement tethered caps on beverage bottles in EU markets. This initiative is in response to the upcoming EU Single-Use Plastics Directive, which mandates that bottle caps remain attached to containers to reduce litter. The move demonstrates a proactive approach by these companies to meet environmental regulations and enhance sustainability efforts.

title: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar Invites Fans to #TakeATaste in Newest Phase of ‘Best Coke Ever?’
summary: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar is launching a new "Best Coke Ever?" campaign called #TakeATaste, encouraging fans to protect their Coca-Cola Zero Sugar from others due to its irresistible taste. The campaign uses influencers, a "Security Can" with a motion-detection camera, and playful branding on promotional packs to engage consumers. This initiative, which includes Coca-Cola Zero Sugar Zero Caffeine for the first time, aims to drive cultural conversation and continue the brand's growth.

title: Luis Felipe Avellar es el nuevo presidente de Industria Mexicana de Coca-Cola
summary: Luis Felipe Avellar has been appointed as the new president of the Mexican Coca-Cola Industry (IMCC), succeeding Roberto Mercadé. Avellar will focus on continuity of operations and sustainability strategy for Coca-Cola bottlers in Mexico. He brings extensive experience from various roles within Coca-Cola, including finance in Brazil and a leadership position in South Africa.

title: Sports Drinks Reinvent Themselves, Look Toward Energy
summary: The sports drink market is evolving, with brands like Gatorade and Coca-Cola's Powerade reformulating products and introducing new offerings that blur the lines between sports and energy drinks. Healthier options, performance energy, and functionality are key drivers of growth, as evidenced by the emergence of brands like BioSteel and the increased popularity of caffeinated sports drinks. This shift reflects changing consumer preferences for beverages that offer both hydration and an energy boost.

title: These 3 companies own the U.S. soft drink market
summary: The U.S. soft drink market is primarily controlled by three major companies: The Coca-Cola Company, PepsiCo, Inc., and Keurig Dr Pepper, Inc., which collectively held 92.9% market share in 2021. The article provides an overview of each company, detailing their business models, product portfolios, and financial performance. It also discusses the challenges and risks within the industry, such as evolving consumer health consciousness and rising costs, while highlighting the stable growth and dividend aristocrat status of Coca-Cola and PepsiCo.

title: Taste the Transformation: Coca-Cola and Grammy-Award Winning Artist Rosalía Break Boundaries With Limited-Edition Coke Creation
summary: Coca-Cola has partnered with Grammy-award winning artist Rosalía to launch Coca-Cola® Move, a new limited-edition flavor under its Coca-Cola Creations platform. This collaboration, inspired by Rosalía's genre-bending transformation in music and fashion, includes a striking packaging design and a new single by Rosalía, "LLYLM," which draws inspiration from the drink. Fans can access behind-the-scenes content, participate in a personality quiz for metaverse avatars, and bid on autographed items benefiting the Antonio Gala Foundation through a scannable QR code on the product.

title: Coca-Cola debuts ‘transformation-flavored’ soda in its latest limited-time offering
summary: Coca-Cola is launching a new limited-time soda called Coca-Cola Move, in collaboration with Grammy-award-winning singer Rosalía, as part of its Creations platform. This new drink, like others in the series, is not tied to a specific flavor but rather to a mood, in this case, "transformation." The Creations platform aims to engage younger consumers by offering unique experiences and flavors, generating buzz and encouraging discussion about what the drinks taste like.

title: The Coca-Cola Co. wields the axe to Lilt after 50 years
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has discontinued its tropical soft drink brand Lilt after nearly 50 years, relaunching it as Fanta Pineapple & Grapefruit. This transition was gradually teased with rebranding efforts over the past few months. The new Fanta variants will be available in various sizes, including a zero sugar option, and Coca-Cola European Partners is confident this move will drive future growth for the Fanta brand while assuring loyal Lilt fans the taste remains the same.

title: Earnings Previews: Airbnb, Devon Energy, Livent
summary: This article provides earning previews for Airbnb, Devon Energy, and Livent, detailing their stock performance, analyst ratings, and financial forecasts ahead of their Q4 2022 reports. Airbnb saw a 32% rise despite a 37% decline over 12 months, with strong analyst confidence. Devon Energy showed a 22% stock increase over the past year and maintains bullish analyst ratings due to its generous dividend. Livent's stock rose 23% in 12 months, supported by a production facility expansion and a largely positive analyst outlook, despite a recent drop in lithium carbonate prices.

title: Lilt to get new name after 48 years
summary: Coca-Cola has rebranded its Lilt soft drink, which has been on shelves for nearly 50 years, as Fanta Pineapple & Grapefruit. The iconic "totally tropical taste" will remain the same, but the product will now fall under the Fanta brand. This change has been gradually implemented, with some fans noticing packaging alterations prior to the official announcement.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Joins National Museum of African American History and Culture’s Corporate Leadership Council With $1 Million Contribution
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has contributed $1 million to the Smithsonian’s National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC), joining its Corporate Leadership Council. This expands Coca-Cola's existing support, which includes a $1.25 million founding grant in 2011 from The Coca-Cola Foundation. The company emphasizes its commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, recognizing the Museum's role in preserving African American history and inspiring a barrier-free future.

title: Furious fizzy drink fans fear Lilt has become latest victim of 'cancel culture'
summary: Furious social media users believe the rebranding of Lilt to Fanta Pineapple & Grapefruit is a result of "cancel culture," stemming from historical allegations of cultural appropriation in its 1980s and 1990s advertisements. Coca-Cola Europacific Partners denies these claims, stating that the change is merely a rebrand to bring the drink into the "Fanta family," with no alteration to its tropical taste. The company highlighted that Fanta's significant market value, compared to Lilt's, influenced the decision to rebrand.

title: Femsa venderá sus acciones en Heineken como parte de su nuevo plan a largo plazo
summary: Femsa has announced it will divest its shares in Heineken as part of a new long-term strategic plan. The company aims to maximize profitability in its core businesses, including Oxxo, Coca-Cola Femsa, and its digital division. This move follows a comprehensive review and seeks to simplify Femsa's corporate structure and reduce debt.

title: Will Walmart open wallets? Prices in focus as retailer reports earnings
summary: Walmart's upcoming earnings report will provide insight into American shopper behavior amidst rising grocery prices. Analysts are keen to see how Walmart plans to counteract supplier price hikes and maintain its dominant position in the grocery market, possibly through price investments and private-label offerings. The retailer is expected to show a rise in Q4 sales, driven by higher-income shoppers attracted to its "Everyday Low Price" strategy.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Announces Nomination of New Director and Approves 61st Consecutive Annual Dividend Increase
summary: The Coca-Cola Company announced the nomination of business leader Amity Millhiser to its Board of Directors, with her election expected to expand the board to 13 members. The company also declared its 61st consecutive annual dividend increase, raising the quarterly dividend by approximately 4.6 percent from 44 cents to 46 cents per common share. This consistent dividend increase underscores the company's commitment to returning value to shareholders, having paid $7.6 billion in dividends in 2022 alone.

title: Costa Coffee Announces New CEO
summary: Costa Coffee has announced Philippe Schaillee as its new CEO, effective April 10, 2023. Schaillee brings extensive experience from Groupe SEB and previously Sara Lee Group and Jacob Douwe Egberts Group, with a strong background in marketing and brand building within the coffee and beverage sectors. He will report to Evguenia “Jeny” Stoichkova, president of Global Ventures for The Coca-Cola Company, and will be based in London.

title: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United breaks ground on expansion for bottling plant in South Bibb County
summary: Coca-Cola Bottling Company United held a groundbreaking ceremony for a significant expansion of its South Bibb County bottling plant. This expansion will add approximately 260,000 square feet to the warehouse and create about 50 new jobs, in addition to the 228 existing positions. The company plans to install a new semi-automatic warehousing system called Vertique, aiming to double sales and distribution by 2024.

title: ‘Best Coke Ever?’ Debate Continues in Star-Studded Coke® Zero Sugar NCAA® March Madness® Creative
summary: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar is launching new NCAA® March Madness®-themed creative featuring basketball legends Earvin "Magic" Johnson and Tamika Catchings, alongside comedians Travis Bennett and Dave Burd (Lil Dicky). The campaign, building on the "Best Coke Ever?" platform, highlights the product's taste through playful "take it" scenarios, aligning with the "TakeATaste" global campaign. The initiative will include TV spots, outdoor advertising, sampling, commemorative cans, and experiential activations in Final Four host cities, with Johnson also supporting HBCUs.

title: Coca-Cola Signs As Early Partner for OpenAI’s ChatGPT, DALL-E Generative AI
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has become an early partner for OpenAI's generative AI technologies, ChatGPT and DALL-E, working with Bain & Company to leverage these platforms for marketing and consumer experiences. This initiative positions Coca-Cola as one of the first major consumer goods companies to publicly adopt generative AI for personalized ad copy and imagery. While acknowledging the technology's potential to streamline operations and enhance marketing, the article also addresses concerns regarding AI's current limitations, such as inaccuracies and potential copyright issues.

title: The Coca-Cola Co. pens deal to explore use of AI tools including ChatGPT
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has partnered with management consultancy firm Bain & Co. to explore the integration of AI tools, including ChatGPT, DALL·E, and Codex, into its marketing and digital communication strategies. CEO James Quincey highlighted opportunities to enhance marketing effectiveness and improve business operations through this rapidly emerging technology. Bain & Co. lauded Coca-Cola's ambitious approach to AI adoption within the consumer products sector.

title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners invests in refillable bottling in Germany
summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) is investing over EUR40m (US$42.3m) to enhance its reusable packaging capabilities in Germany. This investment will fund a new filling line in Lüneburg for refillable glass bottles and a new packaging machine for glass bottles in Mönchengladbach. The initiative aims to strengthen CCEP's commitment to sustainable packaging solutions.

title: Femsa sube sus ingresos pero reporta menos utilidades
summary: Femsa reported a rise in total revenue by 23% year-on-year to 186,467 million pesos, driven by growth across all business units, especially its proximity division (Oxxo stores) and Coca-Cola Femsa. However, the company's net profit decreased to 4,817 million pesos compared to 6,717 million pesos in the same period of 2021. Femsa also announced plans to invest 1,700 million dollars in its core businesses after divesting its stake in Heineken.

title: If I'd invested $1,000 in Berkshire Hathaway shares 25 years ago, here's how much I'd have now!
summary: This article explores the hypothetical returns of investing $1,000 in Berkshire Hathaway B shares 25 years ago. The investment would have grown to $8,208.54, an increase of 713%, outperforming the S&P 500. The author also discusses Berkshire Hathaway's current portfolio, Warren Buffett's views on share buybacks, and the company's succession plans as key considerations for potential investors.

title: Starbucks Corp. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Starbucks Corp. stock rose 0.83% to $102.44 on Monday, breaking a six-day losing streak, amidst a generally positive day for the stock market. The company's stock outperformed some competitors like Coca-Cola Co. and PepsiCo Inc. which saw slight declines, though McDonald's Corp. also rose. Starbucks closed $8.39 below its 52-week high, with trading volume below its 50-day average.

title: LVHD Top Holdings List & Exposure (Franklin U.S. Low Volatility High Dividend Index ETF)
summary: This article provides the top holdings and exposure breakdown for the Franklin U.S. Low Volatility High Dividend Index ETF (LVHD). It lists the top 25 stock holdings by weight, which collectively comprise 56.60% of the fund, and details the ETF's geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposures. The fund primarily invests in North American companies with a focus on high dividend yield strategies.

title: EU antitrust regulators scrap investigation into Coca-Cola, bottlers
summary: The European Union's antitrust regulators have dropped an investigation into The Coca-Cola Co and its bottlers, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners and Coca-Cola Hellenic. The probe concerned potential anti-competitive practices, specifically conditional rebates to retailers aimed at blocking new drinks from entering the market. The EU competition enforcer concluded there was "insufficient ground to further pursue the investigation," though clarified this does not mean the conduct complies with EU competition rules.

title: Coca-Cola Co. & botlers escape EU regulatory probe
summary: The European Union has dropped its antitrust investigation into The Coca-Cola Co. and two of its bottlers, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners and Coca-Cola Hellenic. The probe concerned potential anti-competitive practices, specifically conditional rebates offered to retailers in some EU countries. The Commission concluded there were insufficient grounds to pursue the investigation further, though it noted this does not imply compliance with EU competition rules.

title: Yes, Coca-Cola Still Makes Cocaine — But None of It Makes Its Way Into the Drink
summary: Coca-Cola's name derives from its original ingredients: kola nut and coca leaf, the latter being the source of cocaine. While the company removed cocaine from its beverage in the early 20th century, it still contracts with a chemical company, Stepan Company, to import coca leaves. These leaves are decocainized, and the resulting cocaine is legally destroyed, primarily to retain the "Coca" in the brand's iconic name.

title: Fresh produce stars in Mexico’s record 2022 ag exports
summary: In 2022, Mexico's agricultural exports reached a record $50.1 billion, a 12.2% increase from 2021, according to SADER. Beverages, fruits, and vegetables constituted 60% of these exports, with beer, tequila, avocados, tomatoes, bakery products, and fresh strawberries/raspberries being the top contributors. Tequila and mezcal showed the highest growth, surging 31% compared to the previous year.

title: vitaminwater Introduces Two New Flavors and Innovative Reformulation of Zero Sugar Lineup
summary: vitaminwater has introduced two new zero sugar flavors, 'with love' and 'forever you', and reformulated its entire zero sugar lineup to include monk fruit and stevia. These new offerings are part of the brand's "Nourish Every You" campaign, aiming to provide varied nutritional benefits to consumers. The products are now available nationwide and follow previous marketing efforts featuring Lil Nas X.

title: Coke brings world-renowned art to life in ‘Masterpiece’ push
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a new global campaign called "Masterpiece" that integrates classic and contemporary art to promote its core beverage as a source of inspiration. The campaign features a two-minute video where a Coke bottle travels through various famous artworks, digital collectibles, 3D billboards, and an online gallery showcasing emerging artists. This initiative is part of Coca-Cola's "Real Magic" platform and aims to connect with creatives while highlighting the brand's presence in uplifting moments.

title: Sprite to Sponsor Drake’s ‘It’s All A Blur’ Tour Across North America
summary: Sprite has announced its sponsorship of Drake's "It's All A Blur" North American tour, marking the hip-hop megastar's first concert series in five years. This partnership continues a decade-long collaboration between Drake and Sprite, which began with the brand's first multi-national campaign in 2010. The sponsorship also aligns with the 50th anniversary of hip-hop, reinforcing Sprite's long-standing connection to the genre.

title: Los 5 embotelladores independientes más grandes de The Coca-Cola Company
summary: The article identifies the five largest independent bottling partners of The Coca-Cola Company, which collectively accounted for 42% of TCCC's total unit case sales worldwide in 2022. It lists Coca-Cola FEMSA, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners plc (CCEP), Coca-Cola HBC AG, Arca Continental, and Swire Coca-Cola Limited as these key partners. The article also details the extensive geographical operations of each bottler, highlighting their significant global reach.

title: ArcelorMittal to produce torches, cauldrons, rings, agitos in Paris 2024 partnership
